| status

| HF-a
| A buried Nile ("Eonile") canyon, drilled and seismically mapped: base ~1500 m below the surface near Cairo; ~3000 m below the present delta plain near the coast; several hundred m below sea level at Aswan.
| Gvirtzman et al. 2022, Comm. Earth Environ. 3, doi:10.1038/s43247-022-00540-4; review compilations
| D0/D1 (borehole + seismic subsurface observation)
| ACTIVE

| HF-b
| Industry 3-D seismic south of Cairo: an unconformity forming a canyon 9 km wide, 1700–1800 m below modern sea level, incised into hard Eocene limestone, with tributaries and a floor distributary network.
| Mitchell et al. 2026, Palaeogeogr. Palaeoclimatol. Palaeoecol., S0031018226001434
| D0/D1 (direct seismic geometry)
| ACTIVE

| HF-c
| Messinian evaporites in the Mediterranean basin: marine salts up to kilometres thick, amounting to ~5% of the global ocean's dissolved salt.
| drilled evaporite record (DSDP/IODP)
| D1 (drilled thickness; "5% of ocean salt" = computed proportion)
| ACTIVE

| HF-d
| A ~390 km erosion channel from the Gulf of Cádiz (Atlantic) across Gibraltar into the western Mediterranean; >250 m incision on both sides of Gibraltar; continuous, U-shaped in its head — interpreted as cut by inflowing Atlantic water.
| Garcia-Castellanos et al. 2009, Nature 462, doi:10.1038/nature08555; ESR review 2020
| D0/D1 (seismic + borehole channel geometry)
| ACTIVE

| HF-e
| Mechanism of control: the canyon-cutting requires a Mediterranean base-level drop, which requires gateway closure (isolation from the Atlantic); the refilling channel enters from the Atlantic side through Gibraltar. The flood/incision is therefore gateway-controlled — its switch is the Atlantic connection.
| inference forced by HF-a..d geometry
| D2/D3 (observation-forced mechanism)
| ACTIVE

| HF-f
| Refill magnitude: modelled discharge 68–100 Sv (some single-dimension models exceed 100 Sv), duration ~2–16 yr, ~90% of the basin filled in months–~2 yr; the largest known flood on Earth, ~1–2 orders larger than Pleistocene ice-sheet outburst floods.
| CFD/incision modelling (Garcia-Castellanos 2009; subsequent CFD)
| D4 (model output)
| RECORD (P)

| HF-g
| Drawdown amplitude is contested even in the mainstream: estimates span "none to >2000 m"; one 2022 backstripping study restores only ~600 m, implying salt precipitated under 1–3 km of water rather than near-total desiccation.
| Gvirtzman et al. 2022; Mitchell et al. 2026; review
| D4 (reconstruction)
| RECORD (P)

| HF-h
| Absolute age assigned by the mainstream: latest Miocene, ~5.33 Ma (Messinian / Zanclean boundary).
| radiometric + biostratigraphic chronology
| D5 (absolute chronology)
| RECORD (F — firewall, both directions)

Reading (firewall-clean, bidirectional).

- The features exist and are extreme — observed (D0/D1, ACTIVE). A multi-kilometre-relief river canyon (HF-a, HF-b), a kilometre-scale salt giant (HF-c), and a 390 km Atlantic-fed erosion channel (HF-d) are not interpretations — they are drilled and seismically imaged. So the physical reality of extreme hydrological incision + basin-scale catastrophic flooding in the Nile / adjacent Mediterranean system is demonstrated, not posited.

- The control variable is the Atlantic gateway — observed-mechanism (HF-e, D2/D3, ACTIVE). This is the key sharpening of the main hypothesis: a flood/incision episode whose on/off switch is the Atlantic connection is exactly the H-F ↔ H-A coupling the scenario hypothesises, now exhibited in a system we can drill. The coupling is no longer only an internal scenario claim; nature shows one realised instance of it.

- The exciting numbers are held out (HF-f, D4 → RECORD). The "68–100 Sv / largest flood ever" figures are model outputs. They are not used as load-bearing — using them to amplify H-F would be the mirror of the contamination the firewall forbids. They are recorded as context only.

- The absolute age is held out in both directions (HF-h, D5 → RECORD/F). The framework neither asserts ~5.33 Ma nor asserts a recent date. The observables above are date-free: a canyon 1800 m below sea level cut into limestone, and an Atlantic-fed erosion channel, are the same physical objects whatever number is attached to them.

- The mainstream itself is unsettled on the reconstruction (HF-g). Drawdown estimates range from "none to >2 km"; abruptness (gradual vs catastrophic) is debated. This is reported under result-neutrality (Art. 3.3): the interpreted reconstruction is genuinely open even among specialists — which supports holding it at [O], rather than picking the version that flatters either side.

Net: H-F's mechanism — extreme incision + basin-scale catastrophic flood, gateway-controlled — is observed to be physically real (promotable toward [F] for physical permission, Art. 4.3). H-F's identity with the scenario's Flood, its global extent, and its absolute timing stay [O]. No chronology used as input.

## PART 3 — The sharpening: an observed instance of the H-F ↔ H-A coupling, plus an honest scale check

3.1 The coupling, exhibited. The scenario's distinctive structural claim is that the Flood and the Atlantic event are two faces of one destabilisation, not two independent assertions (SCENARIO §"unifying substrate"). The Mediterranean / Nile record gives a real, drilled instance of the abstract structure: a major hydrological event (desiccation-incision then refilling-flood) whose single control parameter is the state of the Atlantic gateway. This does not prove the scenario's specific global Flood; it removes the objection that "a flood gated by an Atlantic-connection change" is a physically strange or unprecedented coupling. It is neither — it is observed. The coupling C1/C2 structure gains an observed-analogue anchor [O→ analogue observed], distinct from proof of occurrence.

3.2 Scale check (cited observables only; no new model). A deliberately conservative, transparent sanity check — is the coupling energetically/volumetrically absurd? (a NoGo screen, not a claim):

- Water source vs. surface ocean. Deep-Earth water on the order of ~1 ocean is observed-plus-inferred to reside in the transition zone (Part 1; budget [O]). A surface flood does not require emptying it — even a small fractional release is volumetrically large relative to surface basins. Screen result: not a STOP. (Releasability remains the open gate, §1.)

- Flood energetics are demonstrably attainable. The Mediterranean refill (HF-d, HF-f) shows nature does drive basin-scale catastrophic floods through a single gateway, at discharges ~1–2 orders above ice-sheet outburst floods. So "a basin-scale catastrophic flood is physically attainable" needs no STOP-level parameter — it is observed. Screen result: not a STOP.

- These screens establish only that the relevant magnitudes are not physically impossible; they do not establish occurrence, extent, or timing. That is the entire permitted conclusion (Art. 0.2).

3.3 What this leaves untouched (scope honesty). The petroleum sub-hypothesis discriminator is unchanged by this module: the decisive test remains the basal-source character of high-latitude source rocks (chaotic till/dropstone at base vs laminated marine shale within fill — oil_model/README, and the prior session's standing). This module strengthens the upstream H-F/S0 nodes; it does not resolve oil origin, which stays the open depth-structure test (next-task A).

## PART 5 — What this module does NOT establish (irreversible scope statement)

- Not a global Flood, and not a dated one. The Mediterranean / Nile observables are a regional system. They are used as (a) a mechanism-reality demonstration (basin-scale catastrophic flood + extreme incision are physically real) and (b) an observed analogue of the H-F↔H-A coupling structure. They are not evidence that a global Flood occurred, nor that any flood was recent. Both stay [O] (SH-4).

- Not a claim against the mainstream chronology. The ~5.33 Ma assignment is held out as forbidden-as-input (HF-h), not asserted false. Independent chronometers remain a declared standing external falsifier for any literal recent reading (Constitution Art. 1.4) — unweakened.

- Not load-bearing on any model number. The dramatic discharge / "largest flood" figures (HF-f) and the drawdown reconstructions (HF-g) are RECORD only. The module would stand identically if those numbers were halved.

- S0 budget and releasability remain open (SH-5). Existence of the high-pressure-water substrate is shown; sufficiency for a surface flood is not.

- Petroleum origin unaffected (§3.3). The basal-character discriminator is still the open, decisive oil test.

M5 (Persian Gulf / mountain-glaciation) and M6 (marine source rock) resolved to "[O] both ways, observable water/geometry retained." Here, identically: the Nile canyon, salt, and channel are retained as observables; the age is [O] both ways.

- Correction Ledger governance/11 Part A: this module is written specifically to not repeat E2/E6 (importing chronology as load-bearing) — the age is RECORD — and to not repeat E9 (overclaiming with a convenient number) — the discharge is RECORD. The one-line guard was applied to every row.

# Module 13 — C1-quant NoGo Screen: Physical Permission of Rapid Warm-Ocean Glaciation (H-F → H-G)

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: Constitution & Blueprint (governance/01), Data Grading Charter (governance/00), C1 mechanism evidence (governance/07), Module 12 (S0/H-F anchors), Master Scenario (SCENARIO_recent_sequence.md §S2).

Status: GATE module. Runs the deferred quantitative NoGo gate C1-quant (SCENARIO §S2: "the continental-scaling quantitative gate, deferred"). Computational; reproducible.

Standing grade: the screen promotes only physical permission of mechanism / rate-capability (Constitution Art. 4.3, Art. 5). Occurrence of any past glaciation remains [O] (Art. 4.2).

Code: c1_quant_screen.py (SEED=19; no RNG exercised; no fitted parameter).

What this module does, in one line. governance/07 grounded C1's mechanism in present-tense physics (Clausius–Clapeyron + observed lake/sea-effect snow). This module runs the deferred quantitative gate: does building a continental ice sheet from a warm-ocean/cold-sky engine require physically absurd (STOP) parameters, or is it permitted — using only measured constants, observed snowfall rates, and present-day measured ice volumes, with no chronology, no reconstructed ice volume, no paleoclimate model.

## 0. The firewall as the screen's operating rule (bidirectional — Art. 3)

A quantitative gate is where "do not be swayed by the average theory" is most easily violated, so the admissibility rule is stated up front:

- Admissible inputs (used): lab-measured thermodynamic constants (Lᵥ, L_f, c_p, ρ); observed present-day maritime snowfall rates (m water-equivalent / yr); present-day measured ice-sheet volumes and thickness (Greenland, Antarctica). All present-tense (Art. 2.1).

- Forbidden inputs (NOT used), in both directions: any absolute chronology — in particular the mainstream "ice ages are paced at ~100 kyr" is not used as a benchmark the fast scenario must beat (that is chronology, governance/11 M3); reconstructed LGM ice volumes (model products); any paleoclimate reconstruction.

- Not load-bearing: no fitted parameter. Every number is a measured constant or an explicitly-ranged assumption, and the screen is run over the range, not at a cherry-picked point.

- Conservative choices (against the scenario, deliberately): the realized water-cycle response (~3.5 %/K, circulation-limited) is used, not the Clausius–Clapeyron ceiling (~7 %/K); the present-day measured (not larger reconstructed) ice volumes are the targets. If the screen passes under these conservative choices, it passes a fortiori.

## 1. The three sub-screens and their results

### Sub-screen A — energy sufficiency

Can the ocean's heat reservoir supply, via latent heat of evaporation, the water to build an observed-scale ice sheet? (The evaporation latent heat is paid by the ocean cooling.)

| Target (present-day measured)
| Ocean-cooling budget required
| Verdict

| One continental ice sheet (Greenland, 2.85×10⁶ km³)
| cool top 1000 m by ~4.3 K, or top 400 m by ~10.8 K
| not a STOP

| (same, shallow layer)
| cool top 100 m by ~43 K
| STOP (layer too shallow)

| ALL present land ice (~30×10⁶ km³) in one pulse
| cool top 1000 m by ~46 K
| STOP (honest)

Reading A. A single continental ice sheet is funded by cooling the upper ~1 km of ocean by a few K — comfortably not a STOP. Building all present land ice in one pulse requires absurd cooling → honest STOP: the scenario must build ice by repeated and/or deeper thermal tapping, not one impulse. (The screen was not rigged to pass everything; it reports the STOP.)

### Sub-screen B — accumulation rate (the scenario's distinctive "fast" claim)

At observed maritime snowfall rates, how long to build continental-thickness ice? Compared against nothing dated.

| Observed snowfall (m w.e./yr)
| Ice growth (m/yr)
| Years to build Greenland-thickness (1670 m)
| Verdict

| 1.0
| 1.12
| 1,491
| fast, not a STOP

| 2.0
| 2.24
| 746
| fast, not a STOP

| 3.0
| 3.36
| 497
| fast, not a STOP

| 4.0
| 4.48
| 373
| fast, not a STOP

Reading B. At observed maritime rates, continental ice thickness accumulates in centuries to ~1.5 millennia → the "fast" claim is not forbidden. The screen makes no comparison to ~100-kyr orbital pacing (chronology, firewalled): it asks only whether the rate is physically attainable, and it is.

### Sub-screen C — moisture enhancement (realized, not ceiling)

A warmer ocean raises evaporation. Using the realized ~3.5 %/K (not the 7 %/K ceiling): an ocean warmer by 3 / 5 / 8 / 10 K raises evaporation by +11 / +19 / +32 / +41 %. Consistent with, and reinforcing, sub-screen B. The lower (realized) value is used throughout.

## 2. Verdict

| Sub-screen
| Result

| A — energy
| PASS / not-STOP for one continental ice sheet (STOP only for "all ice at once")

| B — rate
| PASS / not-STOP — centuries to millennia at observed rates

| C — moisture
| consistent (realized enhancement)

C1's rate-capability is PHYSICALLY PERMITTED (Art. 4.3 mechanism/permission; Art. 5 UNLOCK). The "warm ocean under a cold sky builds continental ice fast" link does not require STOP-level parameters, under conservative (realized-efficiency, present-day-volume) assumptions. Occurrence of any specific glaciation remains [O] — the screen establishes permission, never history.

## 3. Open sub-gates (HOLD — genuinely unresolved, reported not hidden)

The screen is 0-dimensional (budgets and rates). Three physical questions it cannot resolve, kept visible per result-neutrality (Art. 3.3) and to prevent an E7-style overclaim (governance/11):

- (i) Spatial distribution. Observed high snowfall is coastal / narrow-band (lake/sea-effect is localized — the governance/07 caveat). Whether a warm global ocean produces continent-wide accumulation, vs. intense coastal bands with dry interiors, is not shown by a 0-D budget. HOLD.

- (ii) Accumulation vs. melt. Net growth needs the snow not to melt → cold continents (summers non-ablating). But a warm ocean also warms nearby land — a genuine physical tension. Resolution requires a cold, high-albedo atmosphere (the scenario's S1 dust loading), which is itself a scenario premise. HOLD.

- (iii) Conditionality on the warm ocean. The entire screen is run given a warm ocean. The warm ocean's origin (S1 jammed-water latent heat) and magnitude are [O] (Module 12 §1: S0 budget/releasability open). The screen proves permission conditional on S0/S1, not the warm ocean itself. HOLD.

## 5. Consilience with existing governance

- governance/07 grounded C1's mechanism (Clausius–Clapeyron + observed lake/sea-effect snow) and flagged C1-quant as deferred. This module runs that gate and returns not-STOP for permission, while preserving 07's honest caveats (localization, realized-vs-ceiling) as the HOLD sub-gates above.

- governance/11 M3 (orbital pacing): this module honors the firewall by not using ~100-kyr pacing as a benchmark — the screen is chronology-free in both directions.

- governance/11 Part A E7 (the retracted "petroleum is the weak link because maturation needs time"): the same discipline applies here — glaciation rate is shown condition-controlled (heat + moisture supply), not clock-controlled, and the screen avoids the inverse error (it does not claim "proven fast"; it claims "not forbidden").

- Constitution Art. 4.3 / Art. 5: only mechanism/permission is promoted (SH-6 [F]); occurrence stays [O]; the failed-impulse case (all-ice-at-once STOP) is recorded as a finding (Art. 5.3, Falsification = discovery).

## 6. Reproducibility / provenance

- c1_quant_screen.py — deterministic; SEED=19 (convention; no RNG used); no fitted parameter.

- All constants measured and stated in-code: Lᵥ=2.45×10⁶ J/kg, L_f=3.34×10⁵ J/kg, c_p(sw)=3990 J/kg·K, ρ(sw)=1027, ρ(ice)=917 kg/m³, A_ocean=3.61×10¹⁴ m².

- Yardsticks are present-day measured: Greenland 2.85×10⁶ km³ (mean thickness 1670 m), all land ice ~30×10⁶ km³ — not reconstructed LGM values.

- Snowfall band (1–4 m w.e./yr) brackets observed maritime climates; realized intensification 3.5 %/K (not the 7 %/K ceiling).

- Append-only: Module 13. Supersedes nothing.

Module 13 complete. C1-quant gate RUN: rate-capability physically permitted (SH-6 [F]); single-ice-sheet energy budget not-STOP; "all ice at once" honest STOP; accumulation fast (centuries–millennia) at observed rates — chronology-free. Three sub-gates HOLD (spatial, melt, warm-ocean conditionality). Occurrence [O], capped. Firewall held bidirectionally; no chronology, no reconstruction, no ceiling-value, no fitted parameter load-bearing. Falsification = discovery.

# Module 14 — C2 NoGo Screen: Glacial Loading as a Physically Real Trigger of Rupture (H-G → H-A)

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: Constitution & Blueprint (governance/01), Data Grading Charter (governance/00), the parent geodynamics Atlantic-opening engine (void-suction / unjamming; the Ψ_eff > Ψ_y yield gate; the ~3–32 Pa net driving-stress window; the τ ≈ 9 s re-jamming self-limit), Module 13 (C1), Master Scenario (SCENARIO_recent_sequence.md §S3).

Status: GATE module. Runs the deferred quantitative NoGo gate C2 (SCENARIO §5.2: "does glacial mass redistribution deliver enough stress to cross Ψ_y?").

Standing grade: the screen promotes only physical permission of the trigger mechanism (Constitution Art. 4.3, Art. 5). Occurrence of any specific rupture remains [O] (Art. 4.2).

What this module does, in one line. It tests the second causal hand-off of the cascade — can a glaciation episode's mass redistribution trigger the Atlantic rupture? — against a present-tense observable: glacially-induced faulting. The answer is framed honestly as a trigger of an already-loaded (near-critical) system, not a from-scratch fracture, which is exactly the scenario's "shock unjams the loaded spring" logic.

## 0. The firewall as the screen's operating rule (bidirectional — Art. 3)

- Admissible (used): mapped present-day fault-scarp geometry (length, height) caused by deglaciation; the mechanical relationship "ice-load change perturbs crustal stress and reactivates near-critical faults" (observation-forced); ice-load stress from measured ice thickness and density (σ = ρ g H).

- Forbidden (not used), both directions: the absolute ages of the faulting episodes (~9–15 ka, or "less than 600 years," etc.) — named, never load-bearing, in either direction; any reconstructed deglaciation-load history used as a load-bearing input.

- Not load-bearing: no fitted parameter. The inherited geodynamics gate values (Ψ_y window, τ) are carried from the parent volume, treated as inherited thresholds, not re-derived here.

## 1. The observable anchor: deglaciation observably ruptures the crust

| #
| Observation
| proc_grade
| status

| C2-a
| Glacially-induced fault scarps in Fennoscandia: mapped, present-day topographic steps up to ~160 km long and up to ~30 m high, produced when continental ice loads were reduced.
| D0/D1 (mapped scarp geometry; LiDAR/DEM)
| ACTIVE

| C2-b
| These are pre-existing faults reactivated by the advance/retreat stress perturbation — i.e. ice-mass change modulates the crustal stress field.
| D2 (observation-forced mechanism)
| ACTIVE

| C2-c
| Honest mechanical bound: unloading stress alone is generally insufficient to fracture intact rock; it triggers faults already close to failure. So the effect is a trigger of a near-critical (pre-loaded) system, not a from-scratch rupture.
| D2/D3 (mechanism + modelling)
| ACTIVE

| C2-d
| Some scarps record extraordinary single displacements (~30 m), far larger than any historical fault movement in the region; whole-crustal rupture has been related to rebound.
| D1 (measured displacement)
| ACTIVE

| C2-e
| Ice-load stress magnitude: for ice 1–3 km thick, the vertical load is σ = ρ_ice g H ≈ 9–27 MPa (order ~10⁷ Pa). Flexural/rebound stresses are smaller (order ~MPa).
| D2 (forced by measured ρ, g, H)
| ACTIVE

| C2-f
| Absolute ages of the faulting episodes.
| D5 (chronology)
| RECORD (F — firewall, both directions)

Reading. The coupling the scenario needs — a glaciation episode's mass change perturbs the crustal stress field enough to rupture it — is not hypothetical; it is mapped on the ground (C2-a, C2-d). The honest qualifier (C2-c) is not a weakness but a structural match: the rupture is a trigger of an already-loaded system, precisely the scenario's metastable-spring picture (S0 loaded → a shock unjams it). Glacial loading is therefore registered as one physically real instance of the "shock" class that the scenario's S3 invokes (alongside impact or internal stress).

## 2. Applying it to the C2 hand-off (glacial loading → Atlantic engine)

The inherited geodynamics engine ruptures when the effective stress exceeds the yield stress (Ψ_eff > Ψ_y), with a small net driving-stress window and a fast self-limiting re-jamming. The scenario's C2 claim is that glacial loading/unloading supplies the perturbation that crosses Ψ_y for a rift already near criticality.

- Screen result — trigger sufficiency: glacial loading produces stress perturbations (order ~MPa to ~tens of MPa, C2-e) that are observably sufficient to rupture near-critical crust (C2-a/d). Crossing a yield threshold by perturbing an already-loaded system therefore requires no physically absurd parameter → not a STOP.

- The honest conditional (the open part): whether the specific Atlantic rift was near-critical at the relevant moment is [O] — it depends on the inherited engine's pre-loaded state, which is itself a parent-volume premise held open. The screen shows the trigger mechanism is real and sufficient for near-critical systems; it does not show the Atlantic rift was in that state. That is the inherited [O].

- Self-limit inherited: the τ ≈ 9 s re-jamming self-limit (parent volume) keeps any triggered rupture from running away — consistent with a rapid-onset, self-tapering event (mirrors C1's self-limit in Module 13).

## 3. Verdict

C2's trigger mechanism is PHYSICALLY PERMITTED (Art. 4.3; Art. 5 UNLOCK): glacial mass redistribution observably ruptures near-critical crust, so "a glaciation episode triggers the Atlantic rupture" needs no STOP-level parameter — conditional on the rift being near-critical, which is the inherited open premise. Occurrence of the specific rupture remains [O].

This completes the two-hand-off NoGo screening of the climate cascade:

- C1 (warm ocean → rapid glaciation): rate-capability permitted (Module 13).

- C2 (glaciation → rupture trigger): trigger mechanism permitted (this module).

Both hand-offs are physically permitted, not forbidden; both keep occurrence [O]; both rest on present-tense observables (lake/sea-effect snow + observed snowfall rates for C1; mapped glacially-induced faults for C2), with no chronology load-bearing.

## 4. Open sub-gates (HOLD — reported, not hidden)

- Near-criticality of the Atlantic rift. The trigger works on a pre-loaded system; whether the Atlantic margin was near Ψ_y is the inherited parent-volume premise, [O].

- Magnitude matching. A 160-km fault scarp is large but is not an ocean-basin rupture; scaling the observed trigger to a continental-rifting event is an extrapolation (the observed analogue bounds the mechanism, not the scale). HOLD.

- Ordering seam (B.5). The pre-opening glaciation (H-G) vs. the geodynamics volume's post-opening hydrological/glacial responses (P16/P19/P20/P24) remain an unreconciled seam (Constitution B.5; author currently holding). This module does not resolve it.

# Module 15 — Correction & Re-specification of the Basal-Character Test (the high-latitude "slow marine" reading was an over-generalization; the world's largest source rock carries cold-water indicators)

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: Constitution & Blueprint (governance/01), Data Grading Charter (governance/00), Correction Ledger (governance/11 Part A, esp. E8), Oil model (oil_model/README), Blueprint v2 (CASCADE_BLUEPRINT_and_GRADED_LEDGER_v2).

Status: CORRECTION + DATA module. Retracts an over-generalization the assistant made about the decisive petroleum test, brings new firewall-admissible data, and re-specifies the test as multi-dimensional.

Standing grade: occurrence/age remain [O] (Art. 4). This module changes a grading, not an occurrence claim.

What this module does, in one line. The assistant had framed the high-latitude source-rock texture ("laminated marine shale, not chaotic till") as unfavourable to the glacial/flood-rapid reading. The author correctly objected that cold high-latitude glacial systems move slowly and deposit fine laminated mud that looks like slow marine sedimentation — so lamination cannot discriminate. New data confirms more: the world's largest source rock (Bazhenov) carries cold-water indicators. The "unfavourable" verdict is therefore retracted and the test re-specified along three independent axes.

## PART A — Assistant correction (inherits governance/11 Part A format)

### [E10] — Framed "laminated source-rock = slow marine = unfavourable to a glacial/flood origin"

- Claimed (prior session report, and in Blueprint v2): that the high-latitude source rocks (Bazhenov, Kimmeridge) being laminated marine shale rather than chaotic till leans unfavourable to the glacial-transport reading, making the basal-character test "decisive and currently unfavourable."

- Confident because: (a) the unexamined mainstream default that "source rocks are quiet low-energy marine," and (b) a conflation of "glacial" with high-energy chaotic till at the ice front, so that "laminated/quiet" read as "not glacial."

- Retracted because — and this re-commits the project's own E8:

1. E8 (already in the ledger): glacial meltwater carries fine suspended mud that settles in low-energy distal basins (proglacial lakes, glaciomarine shelves), producing finely laminated sediment — varves. Cold high-latitude / slow-moving (cold-based) ice and deglacial meltwater pulses deposit quiet, fine, laminated sediment. So "laminated/quiet ⇒ not glacial" is exactly the conflation E8 already retracted; the assistant partly re-made it.

2. Lamination is a standard glacial facies, hence degenerate. Glaciolacustrine and glaciomarine sediments are typically laminated on the millimetre scale; "laminated, normal-graded, conformable, with dropstones" are interpretation criteria for both glaciomarine and glaciolacustrine settings. Texture alone does not separate glacial from slow-marine.

3. Empirically wrong for the actual rock (see Part B): the Bazhenov Formation carries glendonites (cold-water mineral pseudomorphs) and a cold-Arctic-shelf geochemical analogue — i.e. the real rock points to a cold high-latitude setting, not the warm low-latitude marine setting the "unfavourable" framing implicitly assumed.

- Status: RETRACTED. The Blueprint-v2 line "the petroleum basal-character test currently leans unfavourable" is corrected to "texture is degenerate; the temperature axis leans cold; rate/transport remain open" (Part C). The error is the same asymmetric mainstream-default failure mode the ledger's root-cause names (governance/11).

## PART B — New firewall-admissible data (graded)

| #
| Observation
| proc_grade
| status

| OC-a
| Glendonites in the Bazhenov Formation (West Siberia, Upper Jurassic–Lower Cretaceous), from the deepest parts of the paleobasin — pseudomorphs after ikaite (CaCO₃·6H₂O), a mineral that crystallises near 0 °C. Presence is a direct mineralogical observation.
| D0/D1 (mineral observation)
| ACTIVE

| OC-b
| Cold-paleoclimate reading of those glendonites (stratigraphic distribution tracks Arctic cooling stages in equivalent units). Caveat held: synthetic ikaite has been grown at ~35 °C, so glendonite-as-strict-cold-indicator carries debate.
| D2 (observation-forced, with noted caveat)
| ACTIVE (caveated)

| OC-c
| Cold-shelf depositional analogue: rare-earth-element distributions place Bazhenov deposition on an inner–outer shelf of an epicontinental sea similar to the present Kara Sea / East Siberian Sea (cold Arctic shelves).
| D3 (REE-based reconstruction; grounded but multi-step)
| ACTIVE (cautious)

| OC-d
| Counter-evidence (kept, result-neutrality): the same basin yields marine reptiles and warm-adapted plant taxa, arguing against a permanent ice sheet — the climate was fluctuating/cool, not a continuous glaciation.
| D1 (fossil observation)
| ACTIVE

| Paleolatitude / absolute age of the basin (Late Jurassic, high-northern reconstruction).
| D5 (chronology + plate reconstruction)
| RECORD (F — firewall, both directions)

Reading. The casual "warm anoxic marine" picture of the world's largest source rock is not what the rock's own minerals say: glendonites (OC-a/b) and a Kara-Sea-type analogue (OC-c) indicate a cold, high-latitude shelf. That removes the basis for calling the texture "unfavourable." But the counter-evidence (OC-d) keeps it honest: this reads as a cool, fluctuating high-latitude sea, not a demonstrated ice age.

## PART C — The basal-character test, re-specified as THREE independent axes (the multi-dimensional view)

The author's point is that a single texture label collapses several distinct physical questions. Separating them:

| Axis
| Question
| Current reading
| Discriminating power

| 1. Texture (lamination)
| laminated vs chaotic
| DEGENERATE — cold/quiet glacial meltwater and slow marine both produce fine laminae
| none (cannot adjudicate)

| 2. Temperature
| warm vs cold water
| leans COLD — glendonites + Kara-Sea analogue (OC-a/c); caveated by warm fossils (OC-d)
| supports the high-latitude-cold framing — but cold ≠ glacial-transport ≠ rapid

| 3. Rate & transport
| slow pelagic vs rapid glacial/flood delivery; ice-transported vs not
| OPEN — temperature indicators do not constrain rate; texture is degenerate
| the decisive axis, and it is unrun

The sharper test that axis 3 demands (the real next experiment). Lamination is degenerate, but dropstones / ice-rafted debris are a positive glacial-transport signal that slow pelagic marine sedimentation cannot produce (outsized clasts dropped from melting icebergs, deforming the laminae beneath them). So the re-specified discriminator is not "laminated vs chaotic" but:

Do the high-latitude source-rock laminae contain dropstones / ice-rafted debris (and what is the grain sorting / provenance)? Presence ⇒ ice transport (supports glacial delivery). Absence ⇒ consistent with either cold-marine-slow or non-iceberg meltwater. Plus an independent rate constraint (event-bedding signatures vs continuous accumulation), since temperature says nothing about rate.

This is the genuinely decisive, firewall-clean, observable test — a pre-registered search for IRD/dropstones + sorting + a rate signature in a representative high-latitude source-rock set, not a map and not a texture binary.

## PART D — Honest standing after the correction

- The "decisive unfavourable" signal is withdrawn. It rested on an over-generalization (texture degenerate) and was empirically wrong for the actual rock (which is cold, not warm). This is a correction in the hypothesis's favour on the temperature axis.

- But it is a re-opening, not a confirmation. Cold-water indicators establish cold, not glacial transport and not rapid deposition. The scenario's distinctive claims (rapid; glacier/flood-delivered organics) remain [O]. A cold epicontinental sea with slow organic-rich mud accumulation remains a fully live alternative and is also [O].

- The firewall point is symmetric. The mainstream default "warm marine ⇒ old/slow" was the contaminant here (now stripped); but the inverse "cold ⇒ glacial ⇒ rapid ⇒ recent" would be the mirror contaminant and is not asserted. Temperature ≠ chronology; the absolute age stays [O] both ways.

- Net: the high-latitude source-rock evidence moves from "degenerate map + unfavourable texture" to "degenerate texture + cold-leaning temperature + open rate/transport, decided by an unrun dropstone/IRD + rate test." More interesting, more open, and pointed at a sharper experiment.

- Glendonites in Bazhenov: first-findings literature (Frolovskaya Megadepression, Ryazanian interval); regional Arctic glendonite/cooling studies (Western Taimyr / Yenisei-Khatanga); glendonite-temperature caveat (synthetic ikaite ~35 °C) noted from the Nordic-Seas Eocene literature.

# Module 16 — The Single-Relaxation Theory of the Coupled Cascade (BUILD mode)

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: the VP physics substrate (jammed solid, R19 bistable switch), the parent geodynamics engine, Modules 12–15, Master Scenario.

Mode: BUILD (per author directive). The distinctive structure of the theory is developed first; inputs are kept firewall-clean (no absolute chronology built in); harsh per-link falsification and the occurrence-[O] grading are deferred to a brief closing note, not used as the working mode. The aim is to construct the theory's own geometry and predictions, so a later phase can stress-test a fully-built object.

Thesis, sharpened. The five "events" (flood, glaciation, opening, termination, petroleum) are not five claims and not a sequence of tuned coincidences. They are the single switching transition of one bistable substrate between two stable states — and the entire transition is controlled by one parameter: the mass of jammed-water reservoir that releases. Develop that, and a chain of distinctive, theory-internal predictions follows.

## 1. The theory in one structure: one substrate, two states, one switch, one parameter

The VP corpus already supplies a universal bistable substrate — the R19 switch, ṡ = g·s − s³ + h, with two stable states separated by an unstable threshold. The Recent-Sequence cascade is that switch, realised in planetary water-and-crust:

- State A — "loaded cold greenhouse." Water and heat are held in a high-pressure, solid-like configuration: jammed State-4 water (ice-VII), which the deep Earth demonstrably stores (Module 12). This is a metastable well — a loaded spring. It is stable until perturbed past threshold.

- State B — "unloaded new equilibrium." Water released to the surface, heat dissipated, the crust reconfigured, the spring spent. A second stable well.

- The switch (h crosses threshold). A shock — impact, internal stress, or glacial loading — pushes the system over the unstable ridge. The transition is not gradual drift; it is a relaxation down the potential, fast at first (steep gradient) and self-tapering as it approaches the new well.

The single controlling parameter. The amplitude of everything that follows is set by how much reservoir releases — call it the release mass. One number, fixed at the switch, sets the flood volume, the ocean warming, the ice built, the loading that triggers rupture, and the heat that closes the loop. This is the theory's defining economy: a one-parameter relaxation, not a five-parameter coincidence.

## 2. The engine: why one destabilisation does three things at once

The power of the substrate is that a single jammed-water destabilisation has three simultaneous mechanical consequences — it does not cause three later events, it is all three:

- Water out → Flood. Losing confining pressure melts the high-pressure ice (depressurisation of ice-VII → liquid, present-tense observable). The water floods out. Total water conserved; only its state changes (State 4 → liquid).

- Energy out → Warm ocean. The release dissipates the loaded spring's stored energy — gravitational (a vast water mass redistributing and dropping in level) plus the configurational energy of the unjamming transition — as heat in the released water. The ocean is left warm, under a dust-laden cold sky. This pairing is not a separate event; it is the same release seen thermally.

- Support gone → Rupture. The rigid State-4 enclosure that was holding a void open collapses when its connectivity is lost (it cannot pass through the forbidden intermediate state, so it fails geometrically), opening a void that the inherited void-suction / unjamming engine drives into a rupture.

So flood, warm-ocean fuel, and rupture trigger are one event read three ways. The cascade then chains these into glaciation and termination. The theory's job from here is to develop the hand-offs and extract the distinctive predictions.

## 3. The coupled chain as one connected system (developing the hand-offs)

Each stage manufactures the next stage's initial conditions — this is the structure a fragmented account cannot have. Developed as a connected system:

release mass ──┬─▶ FLOOD volume
├─▶ OCEAN warming ΔT ──▶ snow flux (C-C × ΔT) ──▶ ICE mass built
│ │
│ ICE loads crust
│ ▼
└─▶ void collapse ───────────────────────▶ RUPTURE (loading crosses threshold)
│
rupture heat + warm circulation
▼
ICE melts ──▶ NEW EQUILIBRIUM

The warm ocean (consequence 2) is the fuel line that feeds the ice engine; the ice mass is the loading line that feeds the rupture; the rupture heat is the melt line that closes the loop. One reservoir release lights all three lines. The chain is self-supporting if the hand-offs balance — and balance is a prediction the theory makes, not an assumption (see §4, P3).

## 4. Distinctive predictions derived from the theory's own logic

These follow from the one-substrate, one-relaxation structure and differ from a fragmented / slow-cyclic account. They are stated as what the theory predicts — the targets a later stress-test will aim at.

### P1 — Coupling co-location (flood ↔ gateway/rifting ↔ glaciation are linked, not independent)

Because one destabilisation drives all stages, the theory predicts their signatures are causally and spatially coupled, not randomly co-distributed. Specifically: a major basin flood/desiccation should be tied to an associated gateway or rifting event, and rapid glaciation should be tied to an associated ocean-warming source. The theory therefore predicts that "a flood whose control knob is a connection/rifting event" is a recurring structure — not a one-off. (One realised instance already exists: a basin-scale flood gated by an oceanic gateway, Module 12.)

### P2 — A single asymmetric pulse (the signature waveform)

Because each stage self-limits — the ocean gives up its heat so the snow engine tapers; the rupture re-jams on a short self-limit — the theory predicts the whole relaxation has a characteristic shape: rapid onset, self-tapering, single pulse, reaching a new equilibrium. This is distinct from a train of evenly-spaced cycles. The theory predicts the record should read as one asymmetric relaxation (sharp start, long taper), with the build phase limited by ocean-heat supply and the termination phase faster (P3).

### P3 — Energy closure with a build/melt asymmetry (a quantitative structural prediction)

The same reservoir funds both building and melting the ice — and the theory predicts how they relate. Building ice goes through evaporation (the ocean pays the latent heat of vaporisation); melting it back pays only the latent heat of fusion. Since vaporisation costs several times more than fusion, the theory predicts a built-in asymmetry: initiation is the expensive, ocean-heat-limited phase; termination is energetically cheap once the rupture restores warm circulation. Distinctive consequence: the loop closes with slow-ish build, fast melt — a rapid termination is the theory's natural prediction, not a puzzle. (This also predicts the ice built ≈ a fixed function of the ocean warming, so the magnitudes are linked, feeding P5.)

### P4 — Material co-occurrence (one engine, a specific mineral/rock suite)

One jammed-water release leaves a specific co-occurring suite: evaporites (the flood water's dissolved load concentrating as the system re-equilibrates), organic-rich fine source rock (the flood/glacial fine sediment settling in the new low-energy basins), and rift/volcanic products (from the rupture). The theory therefore predicts these should be found together, in causal association, not as unrelated accidents. (A realised co-occurrence: a basin with a kilometre-scale salt giant, organic-rich shales, and an oceanic-gateway rifting control — Module 12.)

### P5 — One-parameter scaling (correlated magnitudes)

Because one number (release mass) sets every amplitude, the theory predicts the magnitudes correlate across instances: a larger release → a larger flood and a larger ice build and a larger rupture, scaling together. The theory predicts flood magnitude, glaciation extent, and opening rate are not independent knobs but one knob seen in three places — so they should co-vary. This is the sharpest distinguishing prediction from any account that treats the three as separate tunable events.

## 5. The positive consilience case (what one engine buys)

A fragmented account needs separate, independently-tuned mechanisms for: a great flood, a rapid glaciation, an accelerated ocean opening, a rapid deglaciation, and the formation of giant petroleum + salt provinces. The Single-Relaxation theory buys all of them from one substrate switch and one parameter:

- the flood and the opening are the same destabilisation (water-out and void-collapse) — not two events needing a coincidence in timing;

- the glaciation is the thermal face of the flood (warm ocean + cold sky), so it does not need an independent orbital trigger to start fast;

- the termination is the rupture's heat closing the loop — not a separate warming event;

- the petroleum + salt + rift suite is the material residue of the single release (P4).

This is the theory's distinctive virtue: consilience from economy. Five phenomena that otherwise require five mechanisms and a fortuitous ordering become one relaxation of one loaded substrate, with the ordering forced by the hand-offs (each stage makes the next). A theory that explains a suite from one engine, with the order built in, has a structure that a collection of separate mechanisms cannot claim.

## 6. Closing note (deferred grading — brief, per the build rule)

The above is built, not yet stress-tested. Holding the manual's discipline only at the end:

- Inputs stayed firewall-clean: no absolute chronology was used as a load-bearing input anywhere in the construction; the realised instances cited are present-tense observables; the predictions are derived from the substrate's internal mechanics.

- Occurrence remains [O] (Constitution Art. 4): the theory is a physically-structured, predictive hypothesis, not a proof that the relaxation occurred. That cap is permanent and is not loosened by building the theory well.

- The predictions P1–P5 are the stress-test targets for the next phase (the author's planned mainstream stress-test): each is specific enough to be challenged — co-location (P1), single-pulse vs cyclic (P2), the build/melt energy closure (P3), the material co-occurrence (P4), and the magnitude correlation (P5). Building them sharply is what makes them falsifiable.

Module 16 complete. BUILD: the cascade is developed as one bistable-substrate switching transition controlled by one parameter (release mass); flood, warm-ocean fuel, and rupture trigger are one destabilisation read three ways; the chain is self-supporting through hand-offs that each manufacture the next stage's conditions; five distinctive predictions (coupling co-location, single asymmetric pulse, build/melt energy closure, material co-occurrence, one-parameter magnitude scaling) are derived from the theory's own logic, with consilience-from-economy as the theory's signature virtue. Inputs firewall-clean; occurrence [O], deferred to the closing note; P1–P5 are the stress-test targets. Falsification = discovery.

# Module 17 — Whole-Chain Energy Ledger (M7 capstone): the cascade closes under one parameter

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 · Inherits: Modules 13 (C1), 14 (C2), 16 (single-relaxation theory), Master Scenario (M7 gate: "does the full chain close energetically without a STOP?").

Status: GATE module (the chain capstone). Computational; reproducible. Code: chain_energy_ledger.py (SEED=19; no RNG; no fitted parameter).

Standing grade: closure of physical permission under one parameter (Art. 4.3, Art. 5). Occurrence remains [O] (Art. 4.2).

What this module does, in one line. Modules 13–14 showed each climate hand-off is individually permitted. This module runs the whole-chain gate: does the entire cascade — relaxation heat → warm ocean → ice → loading → rupture → melt → equilibrium — close energetically under a single controlling parameter, with no physically absurd step, using measured constants only? It does, and the theory's distinctive build/melt asymmetry (Module 16 P3) falls out quantitatively.

## 0. Firewall (both directions)

Inputs are measured constants and present-day measured yardsticks (ocean area/volume, present ice masses, geothermal flux). No absolute chronology, no reconstructed ice volumes, no paleoclimate model, no fitted parameter. The one free quantity is the ocean heat anomaly (a warm-layer warming), run over a range. Any STOP is reported.

## 1. The result (single parameter = ocean warm-layer anomaly)

| Ocean warming
| Ice built (vs Greenland)
| Build energy
| Melt energy

| 0.14×
| high

Melt time computed at the global geothermal flux — a deliberate upper bound*; a rupture concentrates mantle/volcanic heat locally, so realised melt is faster.

Reading. Across the range, one ocean-heat anomaly builds a fraction of a continental ice sheet (0.14–0.46× Greenland), loads the crust (feeding C2), and the melt is comfortably affordable — the chain closes with no STOP for a single ice sheet. (Building all present ice in one pulse remains the honest STOP from Module 13.) Everything scales with the one parameter — the theory's one-knob economy (Module 16), made quantitative.

## 2. The distinctive prediction, confirmed from measured constants (Module 16 P3)

Building ice goes through evaporation (the ocean pays the latent heat of vaporisation, ~2.45×10⁶ J/kg); melting it back pays only the latent heat of fusion (~3.34×10⁵ J/kg). From these measured constants alone:

Building ice is ~7.3× more expensive than melting it.

So the loop closes asymmetrically: a slow, ocean-heat-limited build, then a cheap, fast melt once the rupture restores warm circulation. Rapid termination is therefore a prediction of the theory, not a puzzle to be explained away — and it emerges with no fitted parameter, purely from two laboratory latent heats. This is exactly the kind of distinctive, falsifiable, theory-internal consequence the BUILD phase aims to produce (Module 16 §6).

## 3. The honest demanding link (flagged for the stress-test)

The source of the ocean heat is the one link the budget shows is demanding. If the heat comes from the gravitational energy of the reservoir release (water redistributing through a ~2 km drop), warming the ocean by 5–10 K requires releasing ~5–11% of the ocean's volume of water. The deep reservoir is ~1 ocean-equivalent (Module 12), so a few-percent release can supply it — large, but not absurd. Caveat held: gravitational potential energy is one source; mantle heat exposed by the rupture and the configurational energy of unjamming also contribute, so this is a sanity bound, not the only path. The flood-energy source is therefore plausible but the demanding link — flagged for the later stress-test, not claimed solved.

## 4. Verdict

The single-relaxation chain is energetically COHERENT under one parameter (Art. 5 UNLOCK at the whole-chain level): it builds ice, loads the crust, and melts back, with no STOP for a single ice sheet, using measured constants only and no chronology. The build/melt asymmetry (rapid termination) is a clean prediction. The flood-energy source is the demanding link, flagged. Occurrence remains [O].

This completes the physical-permission screening of the entire cascade:

- S0 substrate observed (M12) · H-F mechanism observed (M12) · C1 permitted (M13) · C2 permitted (M14) · whole-chain energy closes (this module).

Every link is now either observed or screened not-STOP, and the chain closes as one budget — the theory's "one relaxation" is quantitatively coherent. What remains is evidence-gathering against the theory's distinctive predictions (Module 16 P1–P5) and the later stress-test.

# Module 18 — Evidence for the Coupling Predictions (P4 co-occurrence, P5 co-variation): the South Atlantic pre-salt, and a multi-pathway refinement

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 · Inherits: Module 16 (the five distinctive predictions P1–P5), Module 15 (multi-dimensional / no-over-generalization discipline), Master Scenario.

Status: EVIDENCE module (Roadmap T1.1 + T1.2). Gathers and grades evidence for the theory's coupling predictions. BUILD-then-grade: the realised co-occurrence is presented first; the honest grading (degeneracy, a counterexample-turned-refinement, the still-distinctive part) follows.

Standing grade: occurrence/age remain [O] (Art. 4). Firewall held both directions (the orbital/age numbers are RECORD).

What this module does, in one line. Module 16 predicted that, because one parameter controls everything, the relaxation's products should co-occur (P4) and co-vary in magnitude (P5). The South Atlantic pre-salt — at the very rift where the Atlantic opened — is a spectacular realised case of the co-occurrence; graded multi-dimensionally, it is real but degenerate, it is the arid (not glacial) flavour of the relaxation (a refinement, per the no-over-generalization rule), and it leaves the co-variation as the still-distinctive, still-open test.

## 1. The realised co-occurrence (BUILD: the theory predicts it; here it is)

At the conjugate South Atlantic margins (Brazil: Santos, Campos, Espírito Santo; West Africa: Lower Congo, Kwanza, Gabon), three of the relaxation's products co-occur in one stratigraphic package at the rift that opened the Atlantic:

| Product
| Observable
| proc_grade
| status

| Rifting / opening
| syn-rift horst-and-graben basement; extensional faulting continuing up to the base of the salt; this is the South Atlantic opening rift
| D0/D1 (seismic basement structure)
| ACTIVE

| Organic source rock
| pre-salt/sag organic-rich lacustrine mudstones + carbonates ("super-rich, thickly developed" — e.g. Bucomazi, Guaratiba sag) — the source rocks of a giant petroleum province
| D0/D1 (drilled lithology + geochemistry)
| ACTIVE

| Evaporite (salt)
| an Aptian salt giant up to ~2.5 km thick capping the sag sequence
| D0/D1 (drilled/seismic thickness)
| ACTIVE

| Rate observable
| salt deposition up to several cm/yr (a fast deposition rate, present-tense-style observable)
| D1 (rate from thickness; period attribution excluded)
| ACTIVE

| Volcanic association
| pre-salt volcanics (basalt flows/tuffs), near the Paraná–Etendeka flood-basalt province
| D1
| ACTIVE

Reading. The theory's predicted suite — rift + organic source rock + salt (+ volcanics) — is observed together, at the Atlantic opening itself, drilled and seismically imaged. As a realised instance of P4 (material co-occurrence) and of the broader "flood/opening + petroleum/salt residue" coupling, this is strong and concrete.

## 2. Honest grading — three independent dimensions (the multi-dimensional view, per Module 15)

The author's standing rule (do not over-generalise; look at every axis) applied to this evidence:

### Axis A — does it distinguish the theory? → DEGENERATE

Mainstream rift-basin sedimentology also predicts this suite: rifting makes restricted basins → climate-induced lake-level drawdown → evaporites; restricted anoxic rift lakes preserve organics. Indeed the literature explains the salt by exactly that — "a climate-induced lake-level drawdown generated the shallow-water environments for evaporite precipitation," extension continuing to the base of the salt. So the co-occurrence is observably real but does not separate the single-relaxation theory from mainstream rift sedimentology. Honest verdict: consistent with the theory, supportive of the coupling picture, but not distinctive.

### Axis B — temperature flavour → ARID, not glacial (a refinement, not a defeat)

The South Atlantic salt formed in a warm, arid Aptian setting (evaporative drawdown), not a glacial-meltwater setting. For this instance the evaporite pathway is arid-evaporative, not glacial. This is a counterexample to the glaciation coupling for this case — and, handled per Module 15, it becomes a refinement:

The single relaxation can produce its evaporite/source-rock residue by more than one pathway — arid drawdown (warm rift basins: South Atlantic pre-salt) or cold/glacial restriction (high-latitude basins: Bazhenov, with cold-water indicators, Module 15). The "one engine" has multiple regional expressions set by local temperature/setting — exactly the latitude-dependent, non-over-generalised picture the author has insisted on, and consistent with the open transport origin {glacial, flood, arid, other}.

So the South Atlantic is the arid-drawdown flavour; it supports co-occurrence and rapidity but is not evidence for the glacial coupling — and saying so is the honest, multi-axis reading.

### Axis C — rate → fast observable (supports rapidity; period firewalled)

Salt deposition at several cm/yr and a >2 km salt giant are fast by any measure — a present-tense-style rate observable that supports the rapidity dimension. Held out (RECORD, both directions): the cyclostratigraphic period/duration attributions (e.g. an orbital ~22-kyr-cycle reading, a ~573-kyr total) are D4/D5 chronology — named, not load-bearing, in either direction. The observable (thickness, cm/yr rate) stays; the clock does not.

## 3. The still-distinctive, still-open test: P5 magnitude co-variation

P4 co-occurrence is degenerate (Axis A). The distinctive prediction is P5: because one parameter sets all magnitudes, the relaxation's products should co-vary — bigger extension ⇒ bigger salt ⇒ richer source rock — whereas mainstream treats these as separately-controlled processes and predicts no tight co-variation.

- Suggestive present-tense evidence: the South Atlantic salt giant tracks the central, maximum-extension segment of the opening rift, and asymmetric rifting produced asymmetric salt/oil distributions on the two conjugate margins (Brazil vs West Africa). This hints at extension-magnitude controlling salt/source-rock magnitude — the direction P5 predicts.

- But it is not yet a clean test. A firewall-clean P5 test requires, across multiple rifted/flood systems, measured present-tense magnitudes — extension/opening width, salt volume, source-rock richness/volume — and a check of whether they co-vary (theory) or are independent (mainstream). That dataset is specified, not yet assembled.

This is the genuine next experiment (Roadmap T1.1, sharpened): a magnitude-co-variation test across rift/flood systems, present-tense geometry only, ages held out.

## 4. Honest standing after this evidence

- P4 (co-occurrence): observably real and concrete (South Atlantic pre-salt = rift + salt + source rock, at the Atlantic opening) — but degenerate; supportive, not distinctive.

- Multi-pathway refinement: the relaxation makes evaporites/source rocks by arid drawdown (warm) or cold/glacial restriction — local temperature sets the flavour. The South Atlantic is the arid flavour (a refinement gained by honest multi-axis reading, not a defeat).

- Rate: salt at cm/yr + a 2 km salt giant is a fast observable (supports rapidity); the orbital/duration numbers are firewalled out, both directions.

- P5 (co-variation): the distinctive prediction, with suggestive support (salt giant ∝ maximum extension; asymmetric rift ⇒ asymmetric salt/oil) and a clean test specified but unrun.

- Occurrence/age remain [O]; the inverse contaminant ("salt + rift ⇒ recent") is not asserted.

# Module 19 — Distinctiveness Audit (anti-contamination): which predictions actually separate the theory from the mainstream, and the sawtooth as a parsimony test

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 · Inherits: Modules 16 (predictions P1–P5), 17 (build/melt asymmetry), 18 (co-occurrence degeneracy), Correction Ledger (governance/11).

Status: ANTI-CONTAMINATION audit. Per author directive ("proceed while guarding against contamination by the average theory"), this module separates the theory's genuinely distinctive predictions from the ones the mainstream also predicts (degenerate), so the theory's case rests only on what truly distinguishes it. BUILD-then-grade preserved.

Standing grade: occurrence/age remain [O]. Firewall both directions (absolute durations are RECORD).

What this module does, in one line. It asks of each of the theory's five predictions: does the mainstream predict this too? If yes → degenerate (cannot be load-bearing for distinctiveness). The audit finds that the product co-occurrence predictions are degenerate, the rate/structure predictions are the theory's real edge — and even the cleanest of those (the sawtooth) is a parsimony advantage, not a clean knockout. The honest result: the theory's case is consilience-from-economy, and a clean discriminator is still missing — which becomes the named next challenge.

## 1. The distinctiveness audit (the anti-contamination core)

| Prediction
| Mainstream also predicts it?
| Verdict
| Why

| P1 — flood ↔ gateway/rifting coupling co-locates

| Rifting-makes-restricted-basins-makes-floods/evaporites is standard; the flood+glaciation+opening triple coupling is stronger but chronology-entangled to test

| internal coherence, not a discriminator
| Shows the theory can work; does not by itself separate it from mainstream

The honest finding of the audit. The theory's product co-occurrence predictions (P1-rift-part, P4) are degenerate — the mainstream's ordinary rift processes predict them, so they cannot be load-bearing for the theory's distinctiveness, and leaning on them would be exactly the contamination the directive warns against. The theory's real edge is on the rate / structure / parsimony axis (P3/sawtooth, P5-co-variation, P2-single-pulse) — but each of those is either parsimony-advantaged-not-decisive (P3) or confounded/chronology-entangled (P2, P5).

## 2. The sawtooth as a parsimony test (the cleanest current case, graded honestly)

### The observation (robust, both-sides agreed)

The late-Pleistocene ~100-kyr glacial cycles are strongly time-asymmetric: slow build (inception), fast termination (deglaciation) — the "sawtooth." This is well established in the proxy record. (Grade: the relative asymmetry of the record shape is D1 ACTIVE; the absolute durations — ~100 kyr, etc. — are D5 RECORD, firewalled both directions.)

### What each side says

- Single-relaxation theory: the asymmetry is forced by two laboratory latent heats — building ice pays the (large) latent heat of vaporisation (ocean-heat-limited → slow); melting pays only the (small) latent heat of fusion, aided by restored warm circulation (→ fast). One measured-constant principle, no tuning (Module 17, SH-16).

- Mainstream: the asymmetry arises from nonlinear feedbacks — ice-albedo, CO₂ draw-down/ventilation, ocean stratification thresholds — tuned within the orbital-pacing framework. The mainstream also reproduces the sawtooth, but with acknowledged difficulties: the "100-kyr paradox" (orbital forcing has little ~100-kyr power), the mid-Pleistocene 41→100-kyr transition with no orbital change, and a "causality problem" (a termination appearing to precede its insolation trigger).

### Honest verdict

The sawtooth is NOT a clean discriminator — both frameworks predict it. The theory's advantage is parsimony: it gets the asymmetry from one principle where the mainstream needs several tuned feedbacks that still leave open paradoxes. That is a legitimate scientific advantage (Occam-style), but it is not a falsification-level knockout, and it must not be overstated: the orbital framework remains robust overall; its difficulties are about the details of the 100-kyr cycle, not a collapse. Firewall caution: the theory's prediction is the relative asymmetry (slow build < fast melt) — which is firewall-clean (no absolute dates) — not the absolute 100-kyr period (which is chronology, RECORD).

## 3. Honest standing after the audit

- No clean knockout discriminator exists yet. Every prediction is either degenerate (co-occurrence — mainstream predicts it), parsimony-advantaged-but-not-decisive (sawtooth), or confounded / chronology-entangled (co-variation, single-pulse).

- The theory's real case is consilience-from-economy. It buys flood + glaciation + opening + termination + salt/source-rock + the sawtooth from one substrate switch and one parameter, with no tuning, where the mainstream uses several independent, separately-tuned mechanisms. That is a genuine theoretical virtue (parsimony + unification) — but parsimony is an argument for preference, not a proof, and the cap stays [O].

- The directive is satisfied: the theory is not leaning on contaminated (degenerate) support; its distinctiveness claim is now restricted to where it is real (parsimony on rate/structure), and that claim is stated at its true, modest strength.

## 4. The genuine open challenge (named, not papered over): find a CLEAN discriminator

The honest next target is a prediction where the theory and the mainstream diverge in a firewall-clean, present-tense observable — something the mainstream cannot also produce. Candidates to develop:

- C-1 — a deep-Earth substrate signature. The theory's engine is jammed State-4 water (ice-VII). Does it predict a specific, measurable present-day deep-water distribution or phase-boundary signature that differs from mainstream mantle-water models? (A physics prediction, potentially clean — no chronology.)

- C-2 — an energy-partitioning ratio. One budget predicts fixed ratios among flood / ice / opening energies. If any such ratio is observable in present-tense magnitudes, a match would be distinctive (the mainstream predicts no such fixed ratio). (Sharper version of P5, designed to beat the size confound by using ratios, not absolute sizes.)

- C-3 — the single-pulse vs many-independent-events structure, expressed in a chronology-free observable (e.g. a structural/relational signature of one coupled relaxation vs many unrelated episodes) — the part of P2 that can be tested without the firewalled period.

A clean discriminator on any of these would move the theory from "parsimonious alternative held at [O]" toward a genuinely testable distinction. Until then, the theory stands as a unified, parsimonious, [O]-capped hypothesis — which is exactly what the constitution says it should be (Art. 4.4).

## 5. Re-pointed roadmap (anti-contamination)

- Drop leaning on degenerate co-occurrence (P1-rift-part, P4) as evidence of distinctiveness — keep them only as consistency checks, clearly labelled.

- Concentrate the distinctiveness case on rate / structure / parsimony (P3/sawtooth as parsimony; the energy closure as unification).

- Hunt for a clean discriminator (C-1, C-2, C-3) — the real next experiments.

- Hold the parsimony argument at its true strength: a reason to prefer, not a proof; occurrence stays [O].

# Module 20 — The Structural Finding: why the theory and the mainstream are degenerate on their core distinction (and what that honestly means)

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 · Inherits: Modules 16–19 (the predictions and the distinctiveness audit), Constitution (governance/01, esp. Art. 1.4, 2, 3, 4.4).

Status: STRUCTURAL synthesis. Completes the clean-discriminator hunt (candidate C-1) and draws the honest structural conclusion of the distinctiveness investigation. Principles kept throughout (firewall both directions; raw observation top tier; occurrence [O]; no manufactured distinction).

Standing grade: occurrence/age [O].

What this module does, in one line. Candidate C-1 (a deep-Earth substrate signature) turns out degenerate — the mainstream already has a deep water reservoir, a release mechanism, and its observable signature. Synthesising across Modules 18–20, every examined axis where the theory differs from the mainstream reduces to rate / magnitude / timing, which the project's own firewall caps at [O] in both directions. The honest conclusion: a clean empirical knockout is structurally hard, and the theory's true standing is the [O]-capped, parsimonious, unified alternative the constitution intended — not a defeat, but the designed endpoint.

## 1. C-1 result: the deep-Earth substrate signature is DEGENERATE

The theory's engine is a deep reservoir of high-pressure "jammed" water (ice-VII) that can be released. Checking whether this differs from the mainstream:

| Theory needs
| Mainstream already has
| Verdict

| a deep water reservoir
| transition zone (410–660 km) holds ~0.6–1 ocean of water (hydrous ringwoodite/wadsleyite + free fluid/ice-VII)
| degenerate

| a release mechanism
| dehydration melting at the 410 km discontinuity (the "transition-zone water filter," Bercovici & Karato 2003) releases water as the mantle upwells
| degenerate

| an observable signature of deep water/release
| a low-velocity layer above 410 km (seismically observed, regionally and globally), compatible with ~0.5–1% melt
| degenerate

Reading. The existence, the release, and the observable signature of deep water are all in the mainstream. The theory's deep-Earth claim is not distinctive in kind. Its only difference is, once again, rate / magnitude: a rapid, large, triggered, flood-producing release (theory) versus a slow, steady, small-degree (0.5–1% melt), convection-driven release (mainstream). And that difference is firewalled — absolute rate/magnitude is RECORD, both directions. C-1 yields no clean discriminator.

## 2. The structural finding (synthesising Modules 18–20)

Every axis examined gives the same shape:

| Axis
| Theory says
| Mainstream says
| Distinguishable cleanly?

| product co-occurrence (salt + source rock + rift)
| one relaxation's residue
| rift-basin sedimentology
| No — degenerate (M18)

| glacial sawtooth (slow build, fast melt)
| one latent-heat principle
| tuned feedbacks
| No — parsimony only (M19)

| deep-Earth water reservoir + release
| jammed-water loaded spring
| hydrous MTZ + dehydration melting
| No — degenerate (this module)

| everything else that differs
| rapid, large, single coupled relaxation, compressed timing
| slow, small, independent, deep-time
| rate / magnitude / timing

The pattern is structural, not accidental:

The theory's distinctive content is the rate / magnitude / timing (rapid, large, single coupled relaxation, recent-compressed). The project's own firewall (Constitution Art. 2–4) forbids absolute rate / timing as load-bearing — in both directions. The mainstream's distinctive content is the opposite rate / timing (slow, independent, deep-time). Therefore the theory and the mainstream are degenerate on precisely their core distinction — and that degeneracy is enforced by the project's own governance, not a flaw in the theory. What is left to distinguish them must be non-rate (a new present-tense observable or mechanism), and on every non-rate axis examined the theory has been found degenerate (the same observables, re-interpreted).

This is the deep reason the clean-discriminator hunt keeps returning "degenerate": the theory re-interprets the same present-tense observables under a different organizing principle (one fast relaxation vs many slow processes), and the only axis on which the principles truly diverge — rate/timing — is the one the firewall caps.

## 3. What this honestly means (both sides, no spin)

- It is not a defeat. The Constitution's stated deliverable (Art. 4.4) is "a physics-permitted, falsifiable, [O]-standing hypothesis with a graded evidence ledger — not a proof, ever." The theory has reached exactly that. Built, internally coherent, unified, parsimonious, falsifiable in principle, and honestly capped at [O]. This is the designed endpoint, not a shortfall.

- The theory's genuine standing: a unified, parsimonious alternative that buys flood + glaciation + opening + termination + salt/source-rock + the sawtooth from one substrate switch and one parameter, with no tuning, where the mainstream uses several independent, separately-tuned mechanisms. Its virtue is consilience-from-economy (an Occam-style reason to consider/prefer) — not a proof, and the cap stays [O].

- A clean empirical knockout is structurally hard under the firewall, because the distinctive axis (rate/timing) is firewalled and the non-rate axes are degenerate. The one genuinely remaining candidate is C-2 — a dimensionless energy/magnitude ratio that the one-parameter budget predicts and the mainstream does not (ratios sidestep both the size confound and the rate firewall). C-2 is hard and not yet established; it is left open, not declared impossible.

- The mainstream is not refuted, and is not weaponised. Its deep-water release, its rift sedimentology, its feedback-driven sawtooth are all robust; the theory offers a more economical reading of the same facts, held at [O].

## 4. Honest implication for the roadmap

- The BUILD phase has reached its natural completion. The theory is built and its distinctiveness is honestly characterised: parsimonious, unified, [O]-capped, distinguished from the mainstream mainly on rate/timing (firewalled).

- C-2 (energy/magnitude ratios) remains the one genuine clean-discriminator candidate worth attempting — but it is hard and may hit the same firewall.

- The genuinely productive next phases are (a) the author-led stress-test (comparing the built theory to the mainstream on the parsimony/consilience grounds, since a clean empirical knockout is structurally out of reach), and (b) extending the single-substrate framework to new domains — which is where the parsimony argument compounds. (Per author directive, the biological/DNA extension and archaeology are deferred to a later session.)

- What to stop doing: hunting for a clean discriminator on the degenerate axes (co-occurrence, deep-water existence, the sawtooth) — they cannot deliver one, and leaning on them would be the contamination the directive forbids.

## 2. The engine, brought in (now load-bearing, not a pointer)

The cascade now carries the actual mechanism:

- State picture (from VP foundation, Appendix L "4-3-1 state dictionary"). The basal shear zone is granular gouge in State 4 (jammed: load-bearing contact backbone, finite yield stress σ_Y, solid-like) or State 3 (unjammed/liquefied: backbone dissolved, viscous flow). Control variable: mean coordination z vs isostatic z_iso = 2d (= 6 in 3D). Jammed fraction ξ ∈ [0,1].

- Collapse (the "yield gate"). Shear heating drives z → z_iso; at isostaticity the relaxed shear modulus G_relaxed → 0 and the yield stress σ_Y → 0 while bulk modulus stays finite — the load-bearing network is lost before melting (liquefaction by unjamming, distinct from melt). Derived constants (soft-disk jamming, SEED-fixed): φ_jam = 0.840, z_iso = 6 (3D), G_relaxed = 0.068·(z−z_iso), G_Born ≈ 0.20 (finite).

- Three stresses, three roles — the key anti-contradiction (now adopted by the cascade ledger). A hostile reading collapses three physically distinct stresses into a fake "7-orders contradiction." They are not in conflict:

- ΔP ~ 10⁸ Pa — the suction deficit; an energy-input boundary condition (sets W_in = ΔP·A_eff·d).

- τ_res = μ_eff·σ_n ≈ 3×10⁵ Pa — the liquefied friction; the part dissipated as heat (Q_fric = τ_res·A_base·d).

- τ_drive ~ 3–32 Pa — the mean-rate kinematic drive; the viscous stress merely to hold the slow mean creep rate against the liquefied viscosity. Bookkeeping at the mean rate, not slip-burst resistance.

- Motion mode = stick-slip (not slow creep). A liquefied zone cannot creep slowly: V_crit ≫ cm/yr by ~10⁸, dτ/dV < 0 (velocity-weakening) ⇒ stuck-or-fast. Cumulative actual sliding to open a 3000 km half-basin ≈ 69 days at V ~ 0.5 m/s; an apparent 30–92 mm/yr "spreading rate" is that brief slip packed sparsely (duty cycle ~10⁻⁹). "Slow steady spreading" is a time-average artifact of stick-slip.

- Energy ledger (chronology-agnostic). W_in ≈ 3×10²⁶ J, of which the bulk is gravitational PE of opening the basin, and only Q_fric ≈ 3.3% (~10²⁴–10²⁵ J, Chicxulub-class, not a planet-scale thermal pulse) is heat. Conduction alone gives ΔT ~ 596 K @ 3 kyr (melt-order) ⇒ advection is forced — the same over-pressured fluid the low-μ_eff path already invokes — predicting a large, testable hydrothermal throughput (~10⁴–10⁶ km³, ~0.1–10% of basin volume).

- Bounds the cascade now inherits: Ω-NoGo 5/5 PASS (ΔR=25<50 km; ΔP=400<500 MPa; μ_eff=2.2×10⁻³≤10⁻²; h=3 mm≥1 µm; undrained at macro scale); master-scale HOLD (μ_eff≈0.002 needs λ=0.9963, pore pressure within 0.37% of lithostatic; continental d²/W≈36 m does not lab-reproduce → rests on geometry-at-scale).

# Module 22 — DNA Emergence inherited whole and runnable, and why DNA is neutral on the occurrence

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: biology↔history bridge · Inherits: VP DNA interpretation method (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20471407); the animal DNA-Emergence (mammoth/elephant, Neanderthal/human) and the plant DNA-Emergence (cold vs UV), both carried runnable under ../dna_emergence/. Consumes: cascade Modules 12–21.

Status: INHERITANCE + INTEGRATION. Per author directive ("opening this whitepaper, DNA emergence must actually be runnable, so inherit it whole, for verification"). Both sub-packages reproduce from frozen NCBI records, no network, no tuning.

Standing grade: present-tense material [V]; occurrence/timescale [O] in both directions.

One line. The cascade now carries the DNA Emergence as a runnable component, not a citation. The DNA work establishes three present-tense facts in two kingdoms — material is a lineage property, the clock is decoupled from the material, the environment writes to STATE not material — and those same facts make DNA neutral on whether any quiet interval was long or short. DNA removes the standard "sequence proves deep time" objection and refuses to be promoted to positive flood evidence. Symmetrically.

## 1. The inheritance is complete and runnable

../dna_emergence/animal/ and ../dna_emergence/plant/ are full packages (whitepaper, governance, reproducibility map, manifest, modules, repro spine). Each runs from frozen NCBI GenBank records with repro/run_all.py, no network, no fitted parameter (SEED = 19, SantaLucia 1998 LOCK). repro/fetch_ncbi.py re-fetches the raw sequences live. The reader can reproduce every number, which is the point of carrying them here.

## 2. What the DNA emergence measures (present-tense, [V])

- Material (γ) is a lineage/kind property, not an environment property. Animal: mammoth/elephant and Neanderthal/human each read as one material kind (clean partition). Plant: the plastid core machinery is conserved across grasses and nightshades (band centres 1.2821 vs 1.2809; rbcL range 0.0082 across six habitats).

- The molecular clock is decoupled from the material. r(substitutions, |Δγ|) ≈ −0.08 (animal, n = 78) and +0.09 (plant, n = 372). A clock count cannot be read as elapsed time or as material.

- The environment writes to STATE / inventory / dwell, not to the material. Cold (CBF/DREB1) and UV (CHS, UVR8) are different loci; CHS γ tracks lineage (cold barley and warm maize both high because both grasses), not habitat. r(γ, GC) = 0.98–0.998 — γ is a composition measure, which is why it is a lineage signature the environment cannot rewrite.

## 3. The firewall link — DNA does not decide the occurrence, in either direction

The cascade holds the flood occurrence and all absolute timescale [O] (Art. 1–2). The DNA emergence is fully consistent with that and tightens it:

- Because material is decoupled from time (fact 2) and conserved regardless of kind/time (fact 1), a small sequence difference is observed even across mainstream-large divergences (mammoth/elephant). So a small |Δγ| is consistent with any elapsed time and discriminates nothing about duration.

- Therefore DNA is neutral on whether a quiet interval was long or short. It cannot be promoted to positive evidence for a compressed timeline (a flood), and it equally dissolves the opposing "DNA divergence proves deep time" (molecular-clock dating). DNA exits the elapsed-time question in both directions.

- This is the two-edged firewall (Art. 2) applied to sequence: the material/clock channel is removed from the time debate, leaving the duration of any quiet interval genuinely open. The flood, like deep time, is decided — if at all — in the history channel (stratigraphy, sedimentology, dated deposits), never by γ.

## 4. Standing

The DNA emergence is inherited whole and verified. Its present-tense reads are [V]; it adds no occurrence or timescale claim, and it explicitly refuses to let sequence conservation argue for or against a flood. That refusal — symmetric, recorded — is what keeps the cascade's [O] honest where biology meets history.

Grade: [V] for the inherited present-tense reads; [O] for occurrence/timescale, both directions, exactly as the cascade requires.
