# Module 23 — Fossil-count audit: raw counts, no imported model (an open strand)

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: biology↔history bridge (ongoing) · Inherits: Module 22; GOVERNANCE Art. 7. Data: p3k14c global radiocarbon database (Bird et al. 2022), carried under ../fossil_audit/.

Status: OPEN. Per author note ("the DNA-fossil research needs more work"). The counts are settled; their cause is not.

Standing grade: counts [V]; cause [O], symmetrically.

One line. Asked whether human/animal remains are sparse from ~10,000 BP to ~2,300 BC, the audit answers with raw counts only: yes, ancient remains are genuinely sparse in absolute number ([V]), and the count even drops toward the present (the fingerprint of recent under-dating, [V]) — but no causal story (flood, taphonomy, demography) is decided by counts ([O]), and importing one to settle the meaning would itself violate Art. 7.

## 1. The counts (recomputed from source, [V])

Over 179,689 real radiocarbon dates and the 1,795 self-tagged as human remains (../fossil_audit/fossil_counts.py):

- Early-Holocene human-remains dates are single dozens per millennium (e.g. 25 at 9–10k BP, 22 at 10–11k, 13 at 11–12k) versus hundreds at 2,000–5,000 BP (peak 341 at 2–3k). Ancient remains are genuinely sparse in absolute terms — the original observation is correct.

- The count drops toward the present (54 in 0–500 BP; peak at 2,000–3,000 BP). Under uniform dating + more recent people + better preservation the most recent bin should be richest; it is not. This is the fingerprint of recent remains being under-dated — a known-recent skeleton is not ¹⁴C-dated.

## 2. What the counts do and do not establish

- [V] ancient sparseness; [V] recent under-dating signature.

- [L] correcting for the under-dating would raise recent counts and make the ancient/recent contrast larger — consistent with "ancient genuinely sparser."

- [O] DISCOVERED ≠ EXISTING: the database counts dated samples, not existing remains; whether sparseness is true scarcity or preservation/discovery loss is undecided.

- [O] the cause — flood, or low early-Holocene population, or preservation — is not decided by counts. A small ancient population predicts the same sparseness, so counts do not discriminate.

- [O] strong sampling-rate claims (e.g. "0.01% vs 100% dated") need an existence denominator absent here.

## 3. The audit posture (Art. 7, demonstrated)

This module is the recorded case behind GOVERNANCE Article 7. Two errors were made and corrected in the open: a data claim asserted from memory ("densely documented" — wrong; withdrawn after counting), and an interpretation imported asymmetrically (taphonomy installed as the answer while flood was held [O] — corrected by demoting every causal model to [O]). The counts are the only [V] object; all causes route to the history channel.

## 4. Standing — open

This strand is deliberately unfinished. Settled: the counts and their grading. Not settled: an existence-calibrated sampling model and any causal attribution. Both are deferred — to further data and to the history channel — and held open, honestly.

Grade: [V] counts; [L] under-dating direction; [O] existence and cause, symmetrically.

# Module 24 — The audit principle: check the interpretation and the datum

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: constitutional (narrative of GOVERNANCE Art. 7) · Inherits: Modules 22–23.

Status: STANDING RULE, with a recorded live case.

Standing grade: procedural — governs how every other grade is earned.

One line. Nothing is load-bearing because someone says it — not an authority, not a textbook, not a prior model, not this assistant's own memory. Before anything is cited, two independent audits must pass: the interpretation must be earned rather than imported (and held to its grade, symmetrically with its rivals), and the datum must be recomputed from the primary source rather than recalled.

## 1. Two axes, both mandatory

Interpretation audit. An explanatory model — including the mainstream one — is held to its grade and no higher. No external interpretation may be imported to settle the meaning of an observation. A favored and a disfavored interpretation of the same observation get the same grade. If a flood explanation of a pattern is [O], a taphonomic or demographic explanation of the same pattern is also [O]. Removing a disfavored model while quietly installing a favored one as if it were the data is a firewall violation.

Data audit. A data claim is not accepted from assertion, summary, or memory. It is recomputed from the primary source — fetch the records, count, report raw numbers. "Rich / sparse / absent" must be backed by an actual count over actual records. Only the recomputed quantity is [V].

## 2. The recorded case (this conversation, logged so the rule is concrete)

- Data error → corrected. The Holocene record was asserted from memory as "densely documented." Wrong. Loading a real database (179,689 radiocarbon dates) and counting showed early-Holocene human remains are single dozens per millennium. The sparseness observation was correct; the assertion-from-memory was withdrawn.

- Interpretation error → corrected. The sparseness was then explained by importing taphonomic bias as if settled, while the flood explanation was held [O] — an asymmetry. Corrected by demoting every causal model (taphonomy, demography, flood) to [O], leaving the recomputed counts as the only [V] object.

## 3. No exemption for convenience

The rule binds the inconvenient direction as well as the welcome one. A model that supports a desired conclusion is held to [O] exactly as one that opposes it; a remembered "fact" that flatters the framework is recomputed exactly as one that does not. The firewall is two-edged (Art. 2); this audit is the procedure that keeps it so — applied to others' conclusions, to mainstream defaults, and to this assistant's own outputs alike, without omission.

## 4. Standing

This posture is itself part of the constitution (GOVERNANCE Art. 7). The grades elsewhere can be trusted because each claim was checked on both axes: is the interpretation imported rather than earned? and is the datum recomputed rather than recalled? Where a check failed, it is logged in the open — here and in Module 23.

Grade: procedural; this is the rule by which [F]/[V]/[L]/[O] are assigned honestly.

# Module 25 — The bounded flood→rift GAP window (≥100 yr), screened and reproducible

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: Blueprint v2 + Graded Ledger (Modules 12–14); Constitution Art. 2 (two-edged firewall), Art. 4 (occurrence capped [O]); Data Grading Charter (governance/00). Consumes: the SH-12 permission screen.

Status: SCREEN module (physical-permission, same class as the C1/C2 no-go screens). Per author directive ("formally incorporate the ≥100-year window; guarantee reproducibility; remain compatible with the Nile record"). Reproducible: repro/gap_window.py, SEED = 19, double-SHA-256 gate.

Standing grade: gap floor [F] (not-forbidden) · ceiling finite but [O] (inherits SH-5) · occurrence/absolute-date [O], both directions.

One line. The flood (H-F) and the Atlantic expansion (H-A) are not simultaneous: H-A begins at least 100 yr after H-F. This non-immediacy is not assumed — it is entailed by the finite observed snowfall rate (you cannot load the crust instantly). The window is bounded: a firm author floor (100 yr) and a finite ceiling (the chain stays one relaxation only while the flood's heat fuels the snow engine), whose number inherits the flood budget = [O]. Floor and ceiling together restore a binding co-constraint: gap-duration and trigger-load are locked by one snow engine and funded by one flood budget. Occurrence and every absolute date stay [O], firewalled both ways.

## 1. The window, and the firewall stated first

H-F flood ──[ GAP ≥ 100 yr ]── H-A Atlantic-expansion onset
└ C1 ice build → C2 near-critical trigger ┘

|
| Status
| Grade

| Floor = 100 yr
| author-fixed; H-A not immediate
| load-bearing (firm)

| non-immediacy (gap > 0)
| entailed by finite snowfall (§2)
| [F]

| load by 100 yr
| mechanically entailed by floor + engine (§3)
| [F] (Tier-A)

| Ceiling τ_fuel
| finite (one-relaxation requirement)
| [O] (number inherits SH-5)

| "the gap took N yr", "2300/2200 BC"
| absolute chronology
| RECORD (D5, F both ways)

| H-A occurrence / magnitude
| —
| [O] (SH-10, SH-11)

The screen establishes only "not forbidden". It does not establish occurrence, extent, timing, or date (Art. 0.2; M12 §0).

## 2. Non-immediacy is entailed, not assumed — [F]

Observed maritime snowfall is 1–4 m w.e./yr (Tier-A D0/D1). The rate is finite, so instantaneous crustal loading is physically impossible. The minimum gap to build even the smallest near-critical trigger (~1 MPa) is, from repro/gap_window.py:

- σ = 1 MPa → 25–102 yr (4 → 1 m/yr)

- σ = 4 MPa → 102–408 yr · σ = 9 MPa → 229–917 yr · σ = 27 MPa → 688–2752 yr

So gap > 0 follows directly from the finite snowfall rate, and the author floor of ≥100 yr sits at the conservative (1 m/yr) end of the rate-limited minimum for a ~1 MPa trigger. "Flood, then a wait, then rupture" is mechanism, not narrative.

## 3. What the floor mechanically guarantees — [F]

Floor + the snow engine forces a minimum accumulated load by 100 yr (recomputed, not asserted):

- 1 m/yr → 109 m ice → 0.98 MPa · 4 m/yr → 436 m ice → 3.92 MPa

By the time 100 yr have elapsed, ~1–4 MPa of basal load is already present — the near-critical-trigger regime. The floor therefore delivers its own trigger budget.

## 4. The ceiling is finite — but its number is [O]

The chain is one relaxation of a loaded metastable state (Blueprint Part 1), not five independent events. It remains "one" only while the flood's latent heat still drives the ocean-warming → snow engine. Once that fuel is spent the engine stops and any further loading would need a different driver — breaking the coupling. Hence a finite ceiling:

τ_fuel = Q_flood / (acc · ρ_w · L_vap)

The extraction rate acc · L_vap is Tier-A (the snow engine removes latent heat at 79–317 W/m² for 1–4 m/yr). But Q_flood is the flood/reservoir budget = SH-5 = [O] (HOLD). Therefore τ_fuel is finite by construction but numerically [O]; pinning it would be an import/overclaim and is withheld. (Raising it from [O] is exactly the SH-5 gate.)

## 5. The restored binding constraint — a co-constraint (one engine, one budget)

This replaces the prior, withdrawn "100 yr forces SH-10" (that was a ceiling property, void under a floor-only spec). The new, stronger constraint:

- One snow engine locks duration to load: σ(MPa) = 9.81×10⁻³ · acc · τ. Duration and trigger-stress are not independent.

- One flood budget funds both the engine's run-time and the ice it deposits (the same evaporated water that cools the ocean is the snow that loads the crust).

So gap and trigger-load are co-constrained by a single parameter — the framework's distinctive one-parameter signature (Module 18 P5 / SH-20 flavour). Clean test: does one flood budget jointly satisfy (a) ≥100 yr of fuel and (b) a trigger-sufficient load? It is decidable once SH-5 is pinned; today it is [O] because the budget is [O].

## 6. Consilience with Module 12 (Nile / H-F) — the compatibility, firewall-clean

The author's requirement that this be compatible with the Nile record holds by construction, and adds no date:

- Orthogonality. The GAP is a relative duration; Module 12's Nile absolute ages (Eonile incision; Zanclean ~5.33 Ma) are D5 = RECORD, firewalled both directions. A duration cannot conflict with held-out absolute ages — the window neither uses nor contradicts any Nile date.

- The Nile anchors the clock's t = 0. Module 12 reads H-F as a discrete, present-tense flood — extreme incision (Eonile canyon, D0/D1) + a catastrophic, rapid refill (Zanclean channel, D0/D1), preceded by a desiccation/loading phase (Messinian salt, D1). A sharp, completed event is precisely the discrete trigger the gap window needs to start at t = 0; the Nile shows the flood not smeared over deep time but as a finished pulse.

- It refines the F↔A coupling, consistently. Module 12's coupling row — "flood and Atlantic event are two faces of one destabilisation", graded [O] — did not assert simultaneity. Module 25 refines it: the two faces are sequential (F then A), separated by ≥100 yr, the flood the Nile-observed earlier face. Refinement, not contradiction.

- Firewall. No Nile date enters as load-bearing. The compatibility is structural (relative duration vs. held-out absolute age), never chronological.

## 7. Reproducibility

repro/gap_window.py — derivation-only, no fitted parameter; Tier-A D0/D1 constants in a single LOCK block (ρ_ice = 917, g = 9.81, ρ_w = 1000, L_vap = 2.50×10⁶, acc = [1,4] m w.e./yr, FLOOR = 100 yr). SEED = 19. Changing any LOCK constant defines a new version. Determinism is proven by a double-SHA-256 self-gate:

2×SHA-256 (ledger body) = 8235bff6fa934b4e4910aac1cf56aa54112a16fed71f0cd2faf9918da3cb6058

python3 repro/gap_window.py → prints the ledger, recomputes the hash, asserts equality (REPRO GATE: PASS).

## Standing — what stays [O]

Occurrence is capped (Art. 4.2): no Tier-A screen promotes H-A's happening above [O]. Module 25 complete. # Module 26 — Reading the post-flood record: taxa, radiocarbon contamination, and the elevation discriminator

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: biology↔history bridge (extends Module 23) · Inherits: Constitution Art. 2 (two-edged firewall), Art. 4 (occurrence/absolute-date capped [O] / RECORD); governance/00 (D0–D5). Data: p3k14c (Bird et al. 2022, public scrubbed/fuzzed cut), frozen subsets under repro/data/.

Status: EVIDENCE + DISCRIMINATOR module. Records a falsifiable test that the author proposed and that the raw data did not support, plus the firewall-neutral contamination arithmetic. Reproducible: three scripts under repro/, each with a double-SHA-256 gate.

Standing grade: raw counts [V]; all ¹⁴C ages D5 / RECORD (both directions); the elevation discriminator [F] (failed/reversed); the reduced reservoir mechanism [V] but non-load-bearing; the flood-chronology reading [O].

One line. Three honest results. (1) The radiocarbon count/taxa record cannot be promoted into a faunal-existence claim — p3k14c is archaeological, not palaeontological (DISCOVERED ≠ EXISTING), the human skeletal records are redacted, and the one abundant animal taxon (bison) is continuous across 2300 BC. (2) The author's elevation discriminator (a genuine falsifiable test) failed: within-region it reverses (Europe/N.America high = older, opposite to prediction), and the global pattern that superficially matches is a Simpson artifact. (3) The contamination arithmetic (firewall-neutral) shows water can shift dates older only via dead carbon and only by hundreds–~2000 yr in carbonate/aquatic settings — never a blanket +7000 yr — while modern-carbon contamination pushes old samples younger. Net: the flood-contamination reading survives only as a small, sample-specific, non-load-bearing correction [O]; absolute ¹⁴C dates remain RECORD, both directions.

## A. The contamination arithmetic — firewall-neutral (repro/contamination_arithmetic.py)

This is instrument physics, true under any chronology (it imports no past-occurrence model). With F_meas = (1-c)·F_true + c·F_contam, age = -8033·ln F:

- Dead carbon (F=0) → OLDER, shift = -8033·ln(1-c), independent of true age: c=5% → +412 yr; c=10% → +846 yr; c≈58% → +7000 yr. To inflate a 4 ka sample to 11 ka requires the sample to be ~58 % dead carbon — not subtle contamination but near-total replacement, flagged by collagen ultrafiltration + C:N screening.

- Modern carbon (F=1) → YOUNGER, and old samples are hypersensitive: a true 40,000 BP sample dates to ~33,000 BP at just 1 % modern carbon, ~23,000 BP at 5 %. So contamination's stronger tendency is to drag old samples toward the present, opposite to "everything pre-flood reads older."

Gate: 2×SHA-256 = faabe48d95a0ad9f432b388d51442fc7bd333f9cf1735c5fd7ab070ac283092b.

## B. Taxa composition — raw counts only (repro/taxa_composition.py)

Over the frozen subset (675 records; ages are RECORD, used only as recorded values):

- Homo sapiens / human: 202 — but the public cut redacts skeletal records; these are coprolite-dominated (DISCOVERED ≠ EXISTING with a third layer, redaction R(t,place)). Present on both sides of 2300 BC, but not a clean test.

- Mammuthus: 42 (mostly one N.America collection) — ages cluster old (median ≈ 10,800 ¹⁴C BP), a few young outliers.

- Mammut/mastodon: ~3 — all ≈ 9,600–11,400 ¹⁴C BP.

- Bison: 425 — ages span the whole range continuously (≈ 65–11,990 ¹⁴C BP), present before and after 2300 BC.

- Elephas/Loxodonta: 0 — a geographic sampling artifact (DB is Americas/Europe-weighted), not a temporal statement.

Reading (firewall-clean). A faunal turnover localised at 2300 BC is not present in the raw counts: bison is continuous across it (a direct counterexample to a universal die-off), and the one taxon that drops out (mammoth) does so at a different ¹⁴C position. Whether the mammoth old-cluster reflects real antiquity, the author's contamination inflation, or sampling — and where it maps under a compressed chronology — is [O], since the ages are RECORD both ways. Gate: 39cd3b8e1a712fe7f6801362fa034f72aa6c81d8e87ce80e56ca625581a237bd.

## C. The elevation discriminator — a falsifiable test that FAILED (repro/elevation_test.py)

The author proposed a genuine, falsifiable prediction: apparent ¹⁴C age should anti-correlate with elevation (high = young, low = old), within a region (caves/dry refuge → less water contamination). Tested on a SEED=19 sample (n = 5,444) with Copernicus DEM elevation:

- Within-region (the requested control): Europe Spearman(elev, age) = +0.214, North America +0.172 — i.e. high = OLDER, the opposite of the prediction (t ≈ 10, 8). Asia/Africa ≈ 0; South America −0.07 (weak, prediction direction, not significant); Australia ≈ 0. Global ≈ −0.03.

- Simpson trap: the global elevation bands superficially match the prediction (0–200 m: med ≈ 3140 BP → 1000–2000 m: ≈ 2315 BP), but this is a region-mix artifact — applying the same-region control the author demanded reverses it.

Reading (honest, both directions). This is not a clean kill: the coordinates are fuzzed/county-aggregated (elevation noise attenuates correlations), and the observed "high = older" is itself the expected settlement pattern (younger lowland agriculture), which is only [O]. So the discriminator does not mechanistically refute the author — it simply fails to support the direction and, where testable, runs opposite. Elevation is a poor proxy for the true contamination driver. Gate: cc9db07edf24be97d664e254f2a54d2ad5ddf41e5a22b8a7d2e1dc64a3e07e60.

## D. What survives, and at what grade

Documented reservoir/hard-water effects are real and go the author's direction (older), but their magnitude is hundreds to ~2000 ¹⁴C yr, confined to carbonate/hard-water settings and aquatic-diet organisms (detected by δ¹³C/δ¹⁵N), and modern AMS pretreatment removes non-reservoir contamination per sample. So the flood-contamination reading is not discarded — it survives as a small, sample-specific, non-load-bearing correction:

- Mechanism ("water/carbonate exposure inflates a sample older; avoiding that water reduces it"): [V] (present-tense, documented — living aquatic organisms date old).

- The author's careful claim ("human samples may be less contaminated by avoiding water"): [O] — not discarded, reasonable.

- The over-scoped versions (elevation proxy / blanket +7000 yr / uniform older): [F] (direction, magnitude, and proxy all fail).

- As load-bearing for the flood chronology: no — the surviving correction is small and sample-specific; absolute ¹⁴C dates stay RECORD, both directions (Art. 4).

## E. The right test, deferred

The correct discriminator is not elevation but carbonate/hard-water context, aquatic vs terrestrial diet (δ¹⁵N), and collagen quality (C:N) — these read the reservoir effect directly. This archaeological DB lacks those sample-level fields, so the question stays [O] here; it needs sample-level data carrying context + isotopes + quality indicators.

Light, hydrogen-rich oil is a loaded spring: at the measured present-day reservoir temperature it thermally cracks to gas + pyrobitumen with a forward lifetime τ(T) that is computed from laboratory kinetics and uses no absolute age. τ collapses steeply with temperature — above roughly 180–190 °C every plausible kinetic choice gives τ far shorter than any deep-time claim, so abundant light oil there puts a heavy preservation burden on the deep-time reading. # Module 27 — Petroleum metastability (I): the oil-cracking clock, and the honest charge-vs-preservation gap

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: Constitution Art. 2 (two-edged firewall), Art. 4 (occurrence/absolute-date capped [O]/RECORD), Art. 7 (audit interpretation and datum); Blueprint Part 5 (the petroleum strand). Supersedes as the petroleum discriminator: the basal-texture test (Module 15), which was a past-deposition question (firewall-awkward, leaning unfavourable) — replaced here by a present-tense observable.

Status: SCREEN module (present-tense metastability, same class as the C1/C2 no-go screens). Reproducible: repro/oil_cracking_clock.py, SEED = 19, double-SHA-256 gate.

Standing grade: cracking lifetime τ(T) = [V]/[F] (present-tense physics) · preservation burden in the high-temperature zone = [F] (forced by kinetics) · the clock as a deep-time-vs-recent discriminator = [O] (escaped by late/continuous charge; see §3) · occurrence and basin age = [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. Light, hydrogen-rich oil is a loaded spring: at the measured present-day reservoir temperature it thermally cracks to gas + pyrobitumen with a forward lifetime τ(T) that is computed from laboratory kinetics and uses no absolute age. τ collapses steeply with temperature — above roughly 180–190 °C every plausible kinetic choice gives τ far shorter than any deep-time claim, so abundant light oil there puts a heavy preservation burden on the deep-time reading. But this is honest both ways: a standalone cracking clock constrains residence since generation, not basin age, and the mainstream escapes it by continuous/recent charge from an old source. The clock therefore becomes a true discriminator only when paired with present-tense evidence that local generation is not ongoing (an over-mature source) and that the accessible volume cannot be resupplied — that pairing is the next task. Occurrence stays [O], both directions; only τ(T) is load-bearing.

## 1. Thesis and firewall (present-tense, not chronology)

The cascade's signature object is a metastable loaded state that relaxes. Light oil is exactly such a state in the petroleum system: a high-hydrogen-to-carbon (high H/C), low-entropy hydrocarbon mixture that is thermodynamically metastable relative to its products (methane + heavier residue/pyrobitumen). It does not introduce a new mechanism — it is the same loaded-spring/relaxation engine, realised in organic matter.

The relaxation rate is the first-order thermal-cracking rate at the reservoir temperature, an Arrhenius quantity:

k(T) = A · exp(−Eₐ / (R·T)) , τ(T) = 1 / k(T)

- T is the present-day measured reservoir temperature — a present-tense observable (drilled, logged).

- A, Eₐ are laboratory-measured kinetics — measured inputs, not fitted (Art. 4.1).

- τ(T) is a forward e-folding lifetime — the analogue of a half-life. It is a property of the system as it is now; it neither uses nor asserts any absolute age.

Firewall compliance (Art. 2, symmetric). τ(T) is present-tense and is the only load-bearing output. The fraction of light oil surviving a residence time is reported only against the dimensionless ratio r = residence/τ, never against an absolute time, so no chronology enters in either direction. The statement "this oil is young" and the statement "this oil is old" are both forbidden; what is graded is the present-tense metastability τ and the burden each reading must then carry. This is the same firewall-neutral posture already used for the radiocarbon contamination arithmetic (Module 26 A).

## 2. The clock (repro/oil_cracking_clock.py)

Representative single first-order oil→gas kinetics (LOCK: Eₐ = 230 kJ/mol, A = 1×10¹³ /s). Real cracking is a distributed-Eₐ process (Pepper & Dodd 1995; Tsuzuki et al. 1999; Behar et al. 2008); this transparent single reaction is calibrated to the empirical oil "deadline" (~150–160 °C over tens of Myr) and is meant as a reproducible screen, not a replacement for compositional kinetics.

| Measured reservoir T
| forward lifetime τ

| 90 °C
| ~3,800 Gyr (effectively eternal)

| 110 °C
| ~72 Gyr

| 130 °C
| ~2 Gyr

| 150 °C
| ~78 Myr

| 160 °C
| ~17 Myr

| 170 °C
| ~4 Myr

| 180 °C
| ~1 Myr

| 190 °C
| ~0.3 Myr

Two facts matter, and one caveat.

(a) The curve is exponentially steep. Below ~130 °C oil is stable for far longer than any geological time — cool reservoirs preserve oil with no difficulty, and the deep-time reading carries no burden there. The metastability argument has no purchase on cool oil and must not pretend otherwise.

(b) There is a robust high-temperature burden zone. Above ~180–190 °C, τ is at most a few million years for every plausible kinetic pair (sensitivity run: at 190 °C, τ ranges only ~0.02–5 Myr across Eₐ = 220–250 kJ/mol). So abundant light oil found at such temperatures is metastable on ≤ Myr scales regardless of kinetic choice — and the deep-time reading must then explain survival over hundreds of Myr. That burden, in the hot zone, is forced [F] and kinetics-robust.

Caveat (honest, Art. 7). Between ~130 and ~180 °C the result is exquisitely sensitive to Eₐ: a 10 kJ/mol shift moves τ by more than ten-fold (at 150 °C, τ spans ~5 Myr to ~2 Gyr across the literature range). So the quantitative burden in the mid-temperature band is not robust; only the hot-zone statement is. This sensitivity is recorded, not hidden.

## 3. The honest plausibility gap — what a standalone cracking clock cannot do

This is the physical weakness the strand must own. The cracking clock constrains the oil's residence since it was generated/emplaced — not the age of the basin or the formation. The two are different quantities, and the mainstream routinely separates them:

In the standard petroleum-system picture, generation is continuous. An old, slowly-maturing source rock keeps expelling fresh oil over geological time; a reservoir can hold recently generated light oil even inside a very old basin. So "hot light oil exists now" is read as "it was charged recently," and the cracking clock is satisfied trivially — the oil is young (short residence) even on the deep-time account, because the rock kept making more.

Therefore, by itself, the cracking clock is degenerate (Module 20's pattern again): both readings satisfy it. The clock measures a real present-tense lifetime [V], but it does not discriminate deep-time from recent — the mainstream escapes through continuous/recent charge. Grading it as a discriminator: [O].

The physical cause of the gap, stated precisely. The escape exists because the source is treated as an inexhaustible, still-active generator. The clock only bites if that escape is physically closed — i.e., if one can show, present-tense, that the local source can no longer be generating the observed oil, or that the observed accumulation cannot be continuously resupplied. Two such closures exist, both measurable and both date-free:

-
Over-mature local source. Source maturity is a present-tense measurement (e.g. vitrinite-reflectance equivalent, biomarker maturity ratios, residual generative potential). If the local source kitchen is past the oil-generation stage (spent), it cannot be currently charging light oil — yet light oil is present and uncracked at temperature. Continuous generation is then physically excluded for that system, and the cracking burden returns in full. The remaining mainstream escape narrows to long-distance recent migration, which carries its own (testable) timing and mass constraints.

-
Volume / mass balance. The total mass of light oil + gas + residue in the accessible accumulation, compared against the source's present residual generative capacity, is a present-tense ratio (no rate, no date). If the accumulated mass exceeds what the present residual source could supply, "trickle re-charge" cannot account for it; a large, single, recent charge is required — which is the cascade's reading, and which the slow-continuous picture cannot give.

Neither closure is a knockout on its own (migration and re-charge histories can be invoked), but each removes one escape, and the convergence — light + hot (short τ) + over-mature local source (no current generation) + large accessible volume (no trickle re-charge) — is what makes the deep-time preservation burden genuinely heavy. This is the same consilience-from-economy logic the rest of the cascade rests on, now applied to one accumulation.

Honest status of the strand after this module: the cracking physics is real and the hot-zone burden is forced, but the strand is not yet a discriminator. It becomes one only with §3.1–3.2 attached. That is the next petroleum task, and it is what "the scenario is under-developed" precisely means here.

## 4. Why this still matters, and why it is worth pursuing hard

- It is the one axis that can break the degeneracy. Module 20 found every other axis degenerate with the mainstream (rate/timing firewalled; non-rate axes re-interpretable). Petroleum metastability is different because the mainstream itself carries a real, acknowledged tension here (the preservation problem of light oil at temperature; oil found where deep-time kinetics predict gas). If §3's closures hold for real systems, the deep-time reading carries a quantified burden that no free re-interpretation removes — a discriminating result the other axes cannot deliver. This is why it is a candidate maximum-strength support, not a weak point, and why it should not be conceded cheaply.

- It frees the strand from the unfavourable texture result. The basal-texture test (Module 15) asked how the source rock was deposited — a past process, and it leaned unfavourable. The metastability clock asks about the present state of the accumulated oil, which is independent of source-rock depositional texture. The Module 15 result therefore does not touch this argument.

- Single-engine economy. No new mechanism: light oil is a loaded spring (metastable high-H/C state) and cracking/leakage is its relaxation — the cascade's universal switch, realised in organic matter.

Changing any LOCK constant defines a new version. Survival is reported only against the dimensionless ratio r = residence/τ. Determinism is proven by a double-SHA-256 self-gate:

2×SHA-256 (ledger body) = a2bcfc0dced80f41dfc3f4007482ec4e77afe89f50aaaa29d43a3a2dd38118ce

# Module 28 — Source-rock organic richness: the burial budget, the dilution paradox, and the cascade's single-event economy

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: Constitution Art. 2 (two-edged firewall), Art. 4 (occurrence/absolute-date [O]/RECORD), Art. 7 (audit interpretation and datum); Module 16 (one-event economy); Module 27 (the petroleum strand, oil-side). Companion to: Module 27 — that module reads the present state of the accumulated oil; this one reads the organic budget of the source rock that made it.

Status: SCREEN module (present-tense mass balance, same class as the C1/C2 no-go screens and the Module 25 snow-rate screen). Reproducible: repro/source_rock_organic_budget.py, SEED = 19, double-SHA-256 gate.

Standing grade: the burial mass balance = [V] (present-tense) · "rich source rock forces three coincident conditions" = [F] (forced) · "those conditions require a catastrophe" = [O] (too strong; sustained anoxia also reaches them) · "one coupled event supplies all three more economically" = [L] (structural; the strongest distinctive card) · occurrence/age = [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. A petroleum source rock is improbably organic-rich: ordinary oxygenated seafloor buries only a fraction of a percent of organic carbon, yet real source rocks carry several to tens of percent. Reaching that forces three conditions at once — a large organic supply, anoxic preservation, and low mineral dilution — and that requirement is firewall-clean and forced. The author's instinct that this is a deep puzzle is correct and quantified here. But two honest points sharpen it into a strength rather than an over-reach: (1) "impossible without a flood" is too strong — sustained anoxic basins (observed today) also reach high organic content slowly; and (2) a naive "a flood dumps the organics" runs into the dilution paradox — fast mineral burial dilutes the organic fraction. The cascade's genuine advantage is not raw catastrophe but economy: a single coupled event delivers all three conditions together — a mass-mortality organic pulse that outpaces mineral dilution, a warm ocean whose decay oxygen-demand self-generates the anoxia, and rift basins that supply the low dilution — whereas the mainstream needs these independent conditions to coincide, sustained, by luck. That economy is the strongest card; it is parsimony, not proof. Occurrence stays [O], both directions.

## 1. The puzzle, quantified (repro/source_rock_organic_budget.py)

Total organic carbon (TOC) is an organic-carbon weight fraction, a present-tense measured property of the rock. The screen is a present-tense mass balance over measured fluxes (organic-carbon rain, burial efficiency, bulk mineral sedimentation) — the same class of input as the observed snowfall rate used in Module 25. No absolute age or reconstructed past rate enters.

TOC = (organic-C rain × burial efficiency) / (mineral flux + organic-matter mass).

Four present-day flux regimes:

| Regime
| resulting TOC

| oxic, open ocean, normal dilution
| ~0.05 %

| anoxic, normal supply, normal dilution
| ~1 %

| anoxic, normal supply, low dilution
| ~6 %

| anoxic, high supply, low dilution
| ~31 %

And the requirement, stated as the dilution constraint:

| to reach TOC
| buried organic-C must be ≥ this fraction of mineral flux

| 1 %
| ~1 %

| 5 %
| ~5.6 %

| 10 %
| ~12.5 %

| 20 %
| ~33 %

Reading. Ordinary oxygenated burial yields ~0.05 % TOC — average shale. Real source rocks carry several to tens of percent. To get there, the buried organic-carbon flux must be a large fraction of the mineral flux — for a rich rock, comparable to the entire mineral input, versus the ~0.05 % of normal background. That is a hundred-fold-and-more enhancement. The author is right: source-rock richness is a genuine, large puzzle, and it is forced by the mass balance.

## 2. The two honest points (Art. 7) — they make the argument stronger, not weaker

(a) "Impossible without a flood/glacial event" is too strong. Sustained anoxic basins exist today (e.g. a restricted, stratified, euxinic basin) and slowly accumulate organic-rich mud; widespread anoxic intervals in the record do the same. So high TOC does not logically require a catastrophe — the bare "you need enhancement" conclusion is shared with the mainstream (its anoxia/preservation school). Grading "requires a flood" as forced would be a firewall breach in the cascade's own favour (the mirror image of trusting a mainstream date). It stays [O]. Holding this honestly is what keeps the rest credible.

(b) The dilution paradox cuts against the naive picture. Note where the mineral flux sits in the mass balance: in the denominator. A catastrophic event that dumps a huge load of mineral sediment would dilute the organic fraction toward low TOC, not high. So "a great flood buries lots of mud, therefore rich source rock" is physically backwards as stated. Fast mineral burial helps preservation (less oxygen exposure) but hurts richness (more dilution) — a real tension the mainstream also faces. A rich source rock needs the organic supply to outpace the mineral dilution, or burial in a low-clastic setting.

## 3. The cascade's genuine advantage — economy and self-consistency, framed correctly

The advantage is not raw catastrophe. It is that a single coupled event supplies, together and from one cause, the three conditions that a rich source rock independently requires — and resolves the dilution paradox by mechanism rather than by luck:

- Organic supply that outpaces dilution. A flood-scale mass mortality delivers an organic pulse far above background primary production — large enough that the organic fraction stays high even with mineral input. This is the dilution-paradox resolution the naive picture lacked: the organic flux dominates, rather than being swamped.

- Self-generated anoxia. A suddenly warmed ocean holds less oxygen and is strongly stratified; the oxygen demand of decaying the mass-mortality pulse consumes the remaining oxygen. The anoxia is produced by the event itself, not imposed externally and maintained by luck. This is mechanistically different from the mainstream's externally-restricted, sustained anoxic basin.

- Low dilution. The rift basins opening in the same relaxation are starved, low-clastic settings — supplying the low mineral dilution the budget demands.

So the cascade buys supply + preservation + low-dilution from one parameter and one event, with the anoxia self-generated and the dilution paradox resolved by an overwhelming organic pulse. The mainstream must have all three coincide, sustained, as independent strokes of luck (the right productivity, the right basin restriction, the right sedimentation, held for a long interval). This is consilience-from-economy — the cascade's signature virtue (Module 16) — and on the source-rock problem it is the strongest distinctive card. It is a reason to prefer, not a proof; it stays [L], and occurrence stays [O].

On the "much fiction" point. The mainstream's per-deposit source-rock stories (which sustained anoxia, which productivity, which restriction, for each rich rock — and, for the world's few giant source intervals, a near-global "oceanic anoxic event" with its own triggered coincidence) are genuinely under-constrained and model-laden. The author's skepticism there has merit. But it is recorded as the mainstream carries a heavy coincidence burden, not as the mainstream is refuted — both occurrences remain [O], and the cascade's claim is the more economical reading of the same forced requirement.

## 4. Where this is testable next (closing toward a discriminator)

Like the cracking clock (Module 27), the bare budget is degenerate; its discriminating power grows when paired with present-tense observations the sustained-coincidence picture struggles to give together:

- Scale and near-synchrony of the world's giant source rocks. A disproportionate share of the world's petroleum is sourced by a few brief intervals. A single coupled event predicts a near-global, near-synchronous, warm-anoxic organic-burial signature; the mainstream predicts independent, basin-by-basin anoxic episodes that happen to cluster. The shared warm-anoxic signature and the geographic breadth are present-tense observables (the relative correlation, not absolute dates). This is the high-leverage test.

- The dilution-paradox check itself. In a candidate rich source rock, is the organic accumulation consistent with an organic pulse that outpaced mineral input (supporting the mass-mortality reading), or with slow accumulation under intermediate sedimentation (the sustained reading)? Present-tense sedimentological and organic-petrographic observables bear on this.

- Couple to Module 27. A rich source rock that is also over-mature (spent) beneath uncracked light oil at temperature ties the two strands: the source can no longer be charging (Module 27 §3), and its original richness demanded the three-condition event (this module). The convergence is the argument.

## 6. Reproducibility

repro/source_rock_organic_budget.py — derivation-only, no fitted parameter; LOCK block of present-day measured fluxes (organic-C rain, burial efficiency, mineral sedimentation, organic-matter/organic-carbon ratio). # Module 29 — Whole-chain consolidation and the honest weak-link report

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: the full Blueprint ledger, Modules 12–28, Constitution Art. 2/4/7. Consumes: the mechanical consistency audit repro/chain_consistency_audit.py.

No new physics; it audits the scaffolding of everything built so far for internal consistency, states each link at its honest strength, and reports the remaining weak links. Per author directive: explain present phenomena better than the competing account, keep internal causality non-contradictory, and leave open what is open rather than forcing it.

Standing grade: the chain is internally acyclic (no circular reasoning) [V]; two internal seams remain open and must be closed; occurrence and all absolute dates stay [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. Mechanically auditing the whole cascade as a dependency graph gives three clean results. (1) The scaffolding has no circular reasoning — it is acyclic. (2) Six claims are unconditionally solid (they rest on nothing open): the high-pressure-water substrate, the gateway-gated flood mechanism, the measured snowfall rate, the engine at laboratory scale, the present-tense oil-cracking metastability, and the forced source-rock richness requirement. (3) Everything else is conditional, and the conditions converge on a small set of open premises — overwhelmingly the reservoir budget / ocean-heat source, then the glaciation premises (net accumulation, moisture reach, the cold-sky), then the rupture-scale premises (near-criticality, continental scaling). These stay [O]; they are not forced, and forcing them would invite the attack the author rightly wants to avoid. Two internal seams (the doubly-specified H-A trigger; the glaciation-vs-post-opening ordering) are the only places the internal causality is not yet consistent, and they must be closed by reasoning. The petroleum strand — the source-rock organic budget — is the strongest distinctive card, framed as economy, not proof.

## 1. The audit (repro/chain_consistency_audit.py)

The cascade is encoded as a graph of claims, each with its grade and what it rests on; the script checks acyclicity, separates unconditional from conditional load-bearing claims, and ranks the open premises by how many load-bearing claims depend on them. Result:

The scaffolding is acyclic — there is no circular reasoning. This is the first thing internal consistency requires, and it holds.

### 1.1 The unconditional solid backbone (state these with confidence)

These six rest on nothing open; they are the genuinely strong, defensible core:

- High-pressure water / ice-VII exists (observed in natural diamonds).

- A gateway-gated catastrophic flood is physically permitted, with the Nile incision + salt + gateway signature observed and drilled.

- The maritime snowfall rate is measured (the input that forces the gap floor).

- The void-suction / unjamming engine reproduces at laboratory scale (39/39).

- Light oil is present-tense metastable — its forward cracking lifetime is a measured, date-free quantity (Module 27).

- Source-rock richness forces three coincident conditions — the mass balance is forced (Module 28).

### 1.2 The open premises the whole chain converges on (leave these [O])

Ranked by how many load-bearing claims rest on each:

| Open premise
| load-bearing claims resting on it
| leave [O] because

| reservoir budget / ocean-heat source
| the most (the dominant root)
| sufficiency is unobserved; pinning it imports a magnitude → forcing it invites attack

Every strong-looking link in the chain (the fast ice build, the gap floor, the glaciation, the C2 trigger, the opening, the termination, even the petroleum economy) is conditional on this set. That is not a flaw to hide; it is the honest shape, and the discipline is to carry these as [O] and let independent work — or nothing — settle them.

## 2. The two internal seams (the only places internal causality is not yet consistent)

These are not evidence gaps; they are places the chain currently says two things. They must be closed for the internal causality to be non-contradictory (the author's hard requirement), and both close by reasoning, with no new data.

- The H-A trigger is doubly specified. One construction has the reservoir release collapse the enclosure and open the rupture immediately; the C2/gap construction has the delayed glacial load trigger it after the floor. Recommended closure: the release primes a near-critical rift (it does not open it), the glacial load is the trigger, and the engine is what drives the opening fast — which preserves the single-switch economy, makes the gap necessary, and is supported by the observed analogue (deglaciation faulting). This promotes near-criticality to load-bearing (its honest cost).

- The ordering seam. The cascade's glaciation is pre-rupture loading; the inherited volume's responses are post-rupture. These are sequential phases of one relaxation, not rival claims. Closure: state the single timeline explicitly and check that no inherited post-opening response requires an ice-free pre-state; if one does, revise the pre-loading magnitude (do not ignore the conflict).

Until these are written, the chain has a real internal inconsistency. They are the first thing to fix.

## 3. The weak-link report (ranked; honest strengths)

Tier 1 — internal-consistency gaps (fix first, by reasoning).

The two seams of §2. A logically inconsistent chain is worthless regardless of evidence, so these outrank every data task.

Tier 2 — the load-bearing open premises (leave [O]; name them so attacks are expected, not ambushes).

The reservoir budget / ocean-heat root above all, then the glaciation premises (net accumulation, moisture reach, cold-sky), then the rupture-scale premises (near-criticality, continental scaling). The correct posture is not to prove these but to state plainly that the chain is permitted if they hold, and that they are open both ways. This is the author's "leave it [O]" discipline applied exactly.

Tier 3 — petroleum discriminators not yet closed (the strongest card, still parsimony).

The source-rock economy (one event supplies supply + self-anoxia + low dilution) is the strongest distinctive claim, but it is [L] — a reason to prefer, not a proof. The cracking clock and the richness budget are real present-tense facts, but as deep-time-vs-recent discriminators they are [O] until paired with the closures (over-mature source, volume/mass-balance, the near-global synchrony of the world's giant source rocks). The present-phenomenon bar the author set — explaining where petroleum is found — routes here: petroleum location co-locating with the cascade signature (rift + salt + rich source) is [L] suggestive, and is the right next test.

Tier 4 — peripheral weak items (state weakly; do NOT lean on them, do NOT let them be the battlefield).

The basal-texture test (leans unfavourable — demoted from "the decisive test"); the elevation discriminator (a real test that failed/reversed, recorded); the mid-temperature cracking sensitivity (kinetics-dependent); and the over-scoped "rich source rock requires a catastrophe" (too strong → [O]). These are correctly weak, and the discipline is to describe them weakly and move on — being attacked on these would be the avoidable, unimportant fight the author warns against.

## 4. What this consolidation establishes

The cascade is internally acyclic, with a small, solid, unconditional backbone, a named set of open load-bearing premises carried honestly as [O], two internal seams that must be closed by reasoning, and one strongest distinctive card (source-rock economy) held at the honest grade of parsimony. The bar is the author's: explain present phenomena — above all the location of petroleum and its associated rift/salt/rich-source suite — more economically than the competing account, while never forcing an [O] above its grade. On that bar the cascade is a live, honestly-graded, internally-consistent-once-the-seams-close hypothesis — exactly the object the constitution prescribes, and nothing overclaimed.

# Module 30 — Closing the two internal seams (forced, not chosen)

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: Module 16 (single-relaxation / R19 switch), Module 25 (the forced gap floor), Module 29 (the audit that flagged the seams), Constitution Art. 2/4/7. Consumes: repro/seam_resolution_check.py.

[v30 update, mark-never-erase: the ordering condition stated in §2 (no inherited post-opening response presupposes an ice-free pre-rupture state) was deferred here for verification; that verification has since been performed in Module 53 — 0 of 8 inherited responses require an ice-free pre-state (one, petroleum, is positively reinforced), so the condition is discharged and SH-41 is promoted from [F]-conditional to [F]. One line. Module 29 found the chain acyclic but flagged two places it still says two things. Both close without new data. The H-A trigger is not chosen — it is forced: the "release ruptures immediately" reading violates the gap floor (rupture would be at time zero, but finite snowfall forces a strictly positive gap), so the only internally-consistent reading is that the release primes a near-critical rift, the glacial load triggers, and the engine drives the opening with the stored configuration energy. ## 1. The trigger seam — resolved by force, not by taste

The conflict (Module 29). One construction (Module 16 §2) has the reservoir release itself collapse the enclosure and open the rupture at the moment of release. The gap/C2 construction (Modules 14, 25) has the rupture triggered by the glacial load built over the ≥100-yr gap. As written, the chain says both.

The resolution is forced. The reading is decided by constraints already sealed elsewhere — not by choice:

- The gap floor is strictly positive, and forced. Finite measured snowfall makes instantaneous crustal loading impossible, so the flood→rupture gap is > 0 (Module 25, gate 8235bff6…). A rupture at the moment of release (time zero) therefore contradicts the gap floor.

- The gap sits between flood and rupture by construction. The rupture must follow the ice load, which itself accumulates over the gap (Blueprint Part 1). An immediate rupture violates this ordering too.

- The release need not rupture to power the opening. In the loaded-spring / R19 picture (Module 16), the release loads the metastable well — it stores configuration energy by removing the enclosure's support; the energy that drives the opening is released when the collapse is triggered, not when the spring is loaded. So "release primes, load triggers, engine drives" loses no energy: the release loads the spring, the glacial load is the perturbation that crosses the ridge, and the relaxation down the potential is the rupture.

The consistency check (repro/seam_resolution_check.py) tests both readings against (1)–(3): the immediate-rupture reading fails (1) and (2); the primes/load-triggers reading passes all three. It is the unique internally-consistent reading. Module 16's "support gone → immediate rupture" wording is therefore demoted to priming language, and the chain is single-triggered.

The honest cost, named and kept [O]. This promotes near-criticality to a load-bearing premise: for the glacial load to trigger the rupture, the rift must be near-critical when loaded (the release having brought it there). This stays [O] — but it is a coherent [O], not a guess:

- "Primed-but-stuck" is a regime, not a tuned point. The inherited engine is velocity-weakening and stick-or-fast: a near-critical zone is stuck until a perturbation unsticks it. The release need only bring the rift into that range of states; any sufficient perturbation (the glacial load) then triggers. No narrow window is required, so no-tuning is respected.

- The "release must be sub-critical (does not rupture alone)" requirement is a one-sided bound, not a fine-tuned coincidence — it either holds or it does not, and whether it holds for the specific rift is exactly the [O].

So the resolution removes the contradiction, keeps the single-switch economy, makes the gap necessary, and is consistent with the observed analogue (deglaciation faulting triggers near-critical faults — load-triggering, not release-rupture). What remains open (was this rift so primed?) is stated as a coherent open premise, not asserted.

## 2. The ordering seam — one timeline under an explicit condition

The conflict (Module 29). The cascade places glaciation before the opening (it loads the crust); the inherited geodynamics volume describes responses after the opening. As written, it was unclear whether these compete.

The resolution. They occupy different positions in one relaxation, so they do not compete by construction:

release (loads the spring)
→ flood + warm ocean
→ [gap ≥ 100 yr : ice builds, loads the crust] (PRE-rupture — the cascade's glaciation)
→ glacial load TRIGGERS the rupture
→ opening
→ inherited post-opening responses (POST-rupture — the inherited volume)

The cascade's glaciation and the inherited responses are on opposite sides of the rupture; one timeline holds both. The seam closes provided one explicit condition, stated rather than assumed:

Consistency condition. No inherited post-opening response may presuppose an ice-free pre-rupture state. None is apparent (the opening dynamics, the thermal relaxation, and petroleum formation do not require the prior absence of ice). This should be verified against the inherited volume's content; if any response is found to require an ice-free pre-state, the conflict is real and the honest fix is to revise the pre-loading magnitude — not to ignore the conflict (Art. 7).

Stating the condition, rather than declaring consistency, is the grounded move: the seam is closed conditionally and checkably, with the failure branch (revise, don't ignore) pre-registered.

## 3. What this closes, and the residue

With both seams closed, the chain is internally consistent: acyclic (Module 29) and single-valued at the trigger and one timeline at the ordering. The internal-causality requirement — that the chain not contradict itself — is now met, conditional only on the stated ordering check.

The residue is honest and small: the resolution names near-criticality as a load-bearing open premise, which now joins the open-premise set of Module 29 (the reservoir budget root, the glaciation premises, the rupture-scale premises). It is carried [O], coherently. Nothing here is forced above its grade; the only thing promoted is a premise's status (from background to load-bearing), not its grade.

# Module 31 — Petroleum location screen on real curated data (where the world's oil actually sits)

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence applications branch) · Inherits: Whitepaper P1/P4/P5 (coupling co-location, material co-occurrence, magnitude co-variation), Module 28 (source-rock organic budget), Constitution Art. 2/4/7. Consumes: repro/petroleum_location_screen.py.

Status: SCREEN module on published curated data — no invented numbers, nothing the reader must supply. It tests the author's standing bar — does the cascade explain where petroleum is actually found, more economically than the competing account? — against the world's giant-field tectonic-setting census and the source-rock concentration census. Reproducible: double-SHA-256 gate.

Standing grade: rifting co-location [V] (a clear majority, ~2× a random null) · few-interval clustering [V] · discrimination [O] (mainstream expects petroleum at rifted margins too) · cascade edge = economy [L] · the single-event reading of the source strand challenged [O] by six relatively-ordered intervals. Occurrence and absolute ages [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. The curated data already exists and is citable. Mann, Gahagan & Gordon (2003, AAPG Memoir 78) classified all 877 of the world's giant oil and gas fields (≈ two-thirds of world reserves) by tectonic setting: passive margin 35 %, rift + sag 31 %, collision/foreland 20 %, other ≤ 14 %. Passive margins are themselves rifted margins, so ~66 % of giant petroleum sits in rifting-associated settings — about twice what a random assignment across the setting classes would give. Sorkhabi (2009) adds that six source-rock intervals (~34 % of the record) hold > 90 % of conventional oil. So petroleum is strongly non-random: concentrated in rifting + salt-bearing margins (Campos, Santos, North Sea, Gulf of Mexico, South Atlantic) and in a few intervals — exactly the suite the cascade predicts (P1, P4). The honest qualifier: the mainstream also expects petroleum at rifted margins (rifting makes the basins, restriction, salt and traps), so co-location alone does not discriminate — the cascade's edge is economy (one event for the whole suite), held at [L], not a knockout. And the six intervals are relatively ordered by superposition — a present-tense fact — so a single event does not straightforwardly explain them; that reading is challenged and must narrow or stay [O].

## 1. The data (already processed, already cited)

Two published censuses do the processing; this module only reads them.

Tectonic setting of giant fields — Mann, Gahagan & Gordon 2003 (AAPG Memoir 78). The world's 877 giant oil and gas fields (≥ 500 million bbl recoverable), ≈ 67 % of world reserves, cluster in 27 regions (~30 % of land). By dominant setting: passive margin 35 %; continental rift + sag 31 %; terminal collision + foreland 20 %; strike-slip/subduction/other ≤ 14 %.

Source-rock concentration — Sorkhabi 2009 (GeoExpro); Klemme & Ulmishek 1991. Six stratigraphic intervals hold > 90 % of conventional oil and gas while spanning only ~34 % of Phanerozoic time.

(For per-basin depth work the USGS World Petroleum Assessment / NAGA — ~170+ basins, downloadable — is the route; not needed for the headline result here.)

## 2. The screen (repro/petroleum_location_screen.py)

- Rifting-associated fraction. Passive margins form by rifting (rift → drift → passive margin), so they and continental rifts are one family: 35 % + 31 % = 66 % of giant petroleum sits in rifting-associated settings.

- Against a random null. If petroleum were placed at random across the ~6 setting classes, any two classes would carry ~33 %. Observed rifting-associated = 66 % → enrichment ≈ ×2.0. The concentration toward rifting is real, not a counting artifact — [V].

- Few-interval clustering. Six intervals holding > 90 % of oil is an extreme departure from uniform — petroleum clusters in a few source intervals — [V].

## 3. Reading — symmetric and honest

What the cascade gets right (present-tense, firewall-clean). The cascade predicts petroleum co-locates with the opening (rifting), with salt, and with organic-rich source rock, all as one engine's residue (P1, P4). The data show exactly that suite: a clear majority of the world's giant petroleum is in rifted margins, and the flagship provinces (Campos, Santos, North Sea, Gulf of Mexico, the South Atlantic conjugate margins) carry rift + salt + rich source together. This is a genuine, curated, present-tense match — [V] for the co-location.

Why it does not, by itself, discriminate. The mainstream expects petroleum at rifted margins for standard reasons: rifting makes subsiding basins, restricted circulation (anoxia + salt), and structural traps. So the co-location is degenerate — both accounts predict it (consistent with the Module 20 structural finding). The cascade's distinctive claim is economy: one event supplies the rift, the salt, the warm anoxic ocean, and the organic pulse together, where the mainstream assembles them over time. That is a reason to prefer (parsimony), not a proof — [L].

The honest challenge to the single-event reading (data vs hypothesis). The source rocks do not cluster in one interval; they cluster in six, and those six are relatively ordered by superposition — a present-tense observable, not merely a set of absolute dates the firewall removes. Six ordered levels are not one event. Per the project's own rule (data conflicts → revise the hypothesis, never the data), the source strand's "single coupled event" reading must narrow — to one engine / one signature (warm-anoxic + rift + salt + organic pulse) that recurs — or be held [O]. It must not be forced. (The cascade's mechanism is untouched by this; what is constrained is only the claim that the deposition was a single episode.) The absolute ages of the six intervals stay RECORD, both directions.

## 4. What this establishes

The author's bar — explain where petroleum is found, better than the competitor — is partly met and honestly bounded. The cascade matches the present-tense location data (rifting + salt + few-interval concentration) and offers a more economical account of why the whole suite co-occurs; that is its strongest distinctive card, at [L]. It does not win on co-location alone (degenerate), and it is challenged on the single-event reading by the six relatively-ordered source intervals — which is recorded, not hidden, and which narrows the claim rather than refuting the engine. Nothing is forced above its grade.

# Module 32 — Reading the material-culture record across the recent horizon: present-tense discontinuities, the Giza singularity, and the synchrony question

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: history↔cascade bridge (extends Modules 23–26, the biology↔history strand, into material culture) · Inherits: Constitution Art. 2 (two-edged chronology firewall), Art. 4 (occurrence / absolute date capped [O] / RECORD, both directions), Art. 7 (audit the interpretation and the datum); governance/00 (D0–D5). Data: frozen tables under repro/data/ (horizon_sites.csv, pyramid_scale.csv), built from primary archaeological/geological literature (sources tagged inline).

Status: EVIDENCE + DISCRIMINATOR module, answering the author-set ★ task in 00_MASTER_SEED.md §7. Records what the material record shows now across the recent ("~2300 BC") horizon, separates the present-tense observables that are load-bearing from the synchrony/cause/rate claims the firewall caps, and logs — at full strength — the present-tense evidence that runs against the strong reading. Reproducible: three scripts under repro/, each with a double-SHA-256 gate.

Standing grade: present-tense discontinuities and continuity counterexamples [V]; the Giza scale/quality peak-then-decline-then-gap [V]; cross-site synchrony [O] (both directions); each discontinuity's cause [O] (both directions); all absolute dates D5 / RECORD; the recent-cascade reading of the horizon [O].

One line. The recent horizon is a real, present-tense signal — but it is a selective one, and it cannot carry a date. Three honest results. (1) A material-culture discontinuity is genuinely present at every site the author names (Giza-era masonry → cruder pyramids → a gap; a flood-silt layer capping the late Liangzhu layer; planned Indus urbanism → "maintenance/squatter" occupation; communal monuments winding down in Britain; Skara Brae abandoned) — these are present-tense facts (superposition, masonry grade, loss of standardisation), recomputed without any date → [V]. (2) But a universal, synchronized collapse is contradicted by present-tense continuity in the same record (Middle & Upper Egypt settlement expands; first-intermediate skeletons show no famine or violence signature; the British Early Bronze Age is vigorous; the Luoyang-Basin Longshan keeps thriving; millet is unaffected) — the archaeological analogue of the bison continuity in Module 26. The change that is [V] is selective (loss of centralised monumental/standardised capacity), not a die-off. (3) Synchrony at a single ~2300 BC instant is [O], both directions: it cannot be built from superposition (an order fact is local to one site), and the only other bridge is the absolute-date column — which the firewall forbids as load-bearing either way; the conventionally-assigned dates themselves span ~600 yr (2500→1900 BCE, RECORD). The recent-cascade reading of the horizon survives exactly where the firewall already places every occurrence claim: routed, intact, to independent geochronology and the history channel — [O].

## A. The present-tense discontinuity census — raw counts only (repro/horizon_census.py)

Over a frozen 12-site table, reporting only present-tense observables (what each record shows now: stratigraphic superposition of an abandonment / squatter / silt / aeolian-sand layer over an occupation layer, a drop in masonry grade, a loss of standardisation, the presence or absence of a famine/violence signature in skeletons). Absolute dates are carried in the table only to test the "one instant" claim; they are D5 / RECORD and bear no weight.

- Six present-tense discontinuities [V] — Egypt (royal monumental masonry lapses; large pyramids cease for ~2 centuries; FIP_record), southern Mesopotamia (river-flow retraction with settlement abandonment along the southernmost Euphrates; PNAS2022), the lower Yangtze (Liangzhu City abandoned, a waterlain silt/clay layer capping the late cultural layer at many excavation sites; SciAdv2021), the Indus (de-standardised "maintenance/squatter" occupation superposed on the planned urban phase; LateHarappan), Britain (large communal-monument construction winding down after the sarsen phase; Neolithic_EBA), Scotland (Skara Brae abandoned, wind-blown sand over the occupation; Orkney). The author's observation is correct: a discontinuity is genuinely there at each site, as a present-tense fact.

- Six present-tense continuity counterexamples [V] — Upper-Egypt towns (Tell Edfu, Dendera) expanding and flourishing, with a possible population increase (NatGeo2021); first-intermediate skeletons showing no famine signature and no violent-death spike (NatGeo2021_Duhig); southern Middle Egypt with settlement continuity and expansion while the delta retracts (PNAS2022); a vigorous British Early Bronze Age (Beaker, metalwork, round barrows) (EBA); the Luoyang-Basin Longshan culture, less affected, continuing to develop and thrive (FourTwoKa); millet cultivation unaffected (FourTwoKa).

Reading (firewall-clean). A universal synchronized collapse is not present in the record: the continuity rows are a direct counterexample, exactly as bison continuity was in Module 26. The change that is [V] is selective — a loss of centralised monumental / standardised capacity — not a die-off. The cause of each discontinuity (flood-aftermath vs drought vs political devolution) is the same observation read three ways and gets the same grade [O] (Art. 7); no reading is imported as the datum. Gate: 0d7ca3f37a27213999c134d2b75ae789e1bf96fc31d26a726c5c472f390ae99d.

## B. The Giza singularity — the author's centrepiece, graded honestly (repro/giza_singularity_screen.py)

The author's strongest claim — "a structure of Giza's calibre could not recur for a long time" — splits cleanly into a part that is load-bearing and a part the firewall caps. A pyramid's surviving design height and its core-construction quality are present-tense measurements; the dynasty order is fixed by stratigraphy/typology (an order fact, not an absolute date).

- [V] The present-tense pattern is real and striking. The 4th-Dynasty Giza/Dahshur giants are the measured peak (Khufu 146.6 m; Khafre 143.5 m; 4th-Dynasty median 104.8 m; all solid dressed stone). The immediate post-peak royal pyramids (5th–6th Dynasty) decline — median 52.0 m, a ×2.0 drop, and rubble cores in 8 of 8. Then a gap: comparable scale does not recur, and when large royal pyramids do return (12th-Dynasty revival, Amenemhat III at Hawara, 58 m), the core is mudbrick — a cruder build, not solid stone. Peak → decline → gap is entirely present-tense → [V]. This is the author's best card and it survives at full strength.

- [O] "Could not recur for a long time" is a duration/rate claim → firewalled both directions.

- [O] The cause. "A catastrophe destroyed the capacity" and "the central funding + bureaucracy that organised the labour force lapsed" are two readings of the same present-tense pattern → same grade (Art. 7); neither is imported as the datum.

- Honest note, logged in the open. Held-out RECORD dates show the masonry decline is a gradual ramp that begins at the 5th Dynasty — i.e. it precedes the "~2300 BC" horizon. That is a present-tense fact (the decline is monotone across the dynasty order, independent of the absolute scale) which weakens, not supports, a single-instant ~2300 BC trigger. Recorded because it is unwelcome to the strong reading. Gate: 8aacf48e49707a713152789fd72715167f45dcc65647b64b4cff8e2fb1409374.

## C. The synchrony question — why it is [O] in both directions (repro/synchrony_window_check.py)

This is the firewall-neutral core of the whole module — an inference-structure screen, true under any chronology.

- [1] Superposition is local. Within one site, a layer above lies later than a layer below — an order fact, present-tense [V]. But "(site X's decline) = (site Y's decline)" is not an order fact: superposition cannot make two sites simultaneous.

- [2] The only bridge to synchrony is the date column — which is D5 / RECORD, forbidden as load-bearing in both directions (Art. 2). The conventionally-assigned dates of the six discontinuities are spread over ~600 yr (Scotland/Britain ~2500 → Mesopotamia ~2154 / Egypt ~2181 → Liangzhu ~2300 → Indus ~1900 BCE).

- [3] Both readings need the firewall-forbidden column. "Compress the spread to one instant ~2300 BC" needs the dates to be wrong in a particular way (RECORD as load-bearing); "the spread is real, the declines are centuries apart" needs the dates to be right (RECORD as load-bearing). The firewall caps both → the material record alone can neither assert nor refute synchrony.

Reading (honest, both directions). Cross-site synchrony at a single ~2300 BC instant is undecided, and is routed — intact — to independent geochronology and the history channel, exactly where Art. 1.3 already places every occurrence/chronology claim. It is not settled by the strong reading, and not refuted by the date-spread. Gate: d9b3b86c281eaf24b0ee0d12126861397d8a9e1da0b6c41f4d8fa6e157f4540a.

## D. The Yangtze card, and the "drought vs flood" tension (recorded, not load-bearing)

The author's lower-Yangtze intuition has a real present-tense anchor: across many excavation sites a silt/clay layer caps the late Liangzhu cultural layer (interpreted as a fluvial or marine flood deposit), and high-resolution cave records register an extreme-precipitation window in the same region (SciAdv2021). The capping layer is exactly the kind of present-tense observable the firewall admits (superposition + sedimentology) → [V] as a local layer. Two honest qualifications, both logged:

- The cause even at Liangzhu is contested. Some workers read the abandonment as flood-driven; others argue weakening began centuries earlier under mid–late-Holocene drought, unrelated to a single flood. Same layer, rival readings → [O] (Art. 7).

- The "4.2 ka" horizon carries opposite hydroclimate signatures — broadly drought in Mesopotamia and Egypt, but flood/wet in the lower Yangtze. A single uniform global hydro-event — one flood or one drought — is therefore in tension with the data both ways. This neither confirms nor refutes the cascade; it caps a uniform global reading at [O] and sends the climate question to independent proxies. The Chinese textual "Great Flood" tradition is a history-channel item, not physical evidence, and is treated as such.

## E. What survives, and at what grade

- The discontinuities ("Giza-era masonry → cruder pyramids → gap"; flood-silt cap at Liangzhu; planned → squatter at the Indus; monuments winding down in Britain; Skara Brae abandoned): [V] — present-tense, recomputed without dates. The author's core observation holds.

- A universal, synchronized collapse: contradicted [V] by the continuity counterexamples — the change is selective (centralised monumental/standardised capacity), the bison-continuity result transplanted to material culture.

- The Giza singularity: [V] as a present-tense peak/decline/gap; [O] for its duration ("long time") and its cause (catastrophe vs funding/bureaucracy collapse), with the 5th-Dynasty onset logged as an unwelcome present-tense fact.

- Cross-site synchrony at a single ~2300 BC instant: [O], both directions — unbuildable from superposition, and otherwise dependent on the firewalled date column.

- As load-bearing for the recent-cascade chronology: no — the material record localises and selects, but cannot date; absolute dates stay RECORD both ways (Art. 4), and occurrence stays [O] (Art. 1.2).

## F. The right test, deferred

The correct present-tense discriminator is not "which sites declined" (that is settled — many did, selectively) but the destruction-layer sedimentology at named sites, read as present-tense lithology: a waterlain, graded silt/sand layer (a flood signature) vs aeolian sand (desiccation/abandonment) vs a burn layer (sack/fire) vs a sterile hiatus (simple depopulation) — discriminated per site by grain-size grading, sorting, micromorphology and diatom/foraminifer content, with independent geochronology carrying the timing. Honest prior: even a real flood-silt layer at one site (as at Liangzhu) is a local [V] and cannot establish global synchrony or a single global event — synchrony stays [O]. This module fixes the present-tense observables; the chronology stays routed off-channel, exactly as the firewall requires.

## G. Raw-proxy audit of the word "drought" (Art. 7, primary file read directly)

A later audit pressed the right question on Part D's phrase "drought in Mesopotamia and Egypt": is "drought" a raw observable, or a causal narrative laid over an observed absence of activity to explain it — i.e. scholars seeing empty cities and reaching for a climate excuse? Art. 7 forbids settling an observation's meaning by importing an interpretation, so the audit is run against the literal primary file, not a recalled summary.

Source, read byte-for-byte. The single proxy most directly tied to the "Mesopotamia drought ~4.2 ka" claim is stalagmite GZ14-1, Gol-e-Zard Cave, Iran (Carolin et al. 2019, PNAS, doi:10.1073/pnas.1808103115; data doi:10.25921/x5zv-ar39, NOAA/WDS Paleoclimatology). The script repro/four_two_ka_proxy_audit.py downloads and parses the untouched NOAA bytes (repro/data/gol_e_zard2019_noaa_RAW.txt, SHA-256 pinned in-gate), so the audit cannot be accused of reading a processed number. Ordering is by depth (a present-tense geometric fact); the age column is printed only as RECORD and is never an input.

The verdict is split, and the split is the point.

- The audit's strong form overshoots. "Drought is a pure invented excuse for empty cities" is refuted by R0: there is a genuine, independently measured observable — the stalagmite's Mg/Ca and δ¹⁸O — recorded by geochemists from cave calcite, not inferred from any archaeological gap. R0 is carried as a present-tense [V].

- The audit's instinct is nonetheless correct, and lands precisely on R3. The climb from a trace-metal ratio to "the drought that caused the regression" is, on the record, the weak rung:

1. the authors' own abstract calls the existence of a coincident climate event still uncertain and pins its entire framing to "settlement abandonment";

2. a >1000-dataset survey (Nature Communications 2024) finds the "4.2 ka event" is not a globally significant excursion (unlike 8.2 ka) and states plainly that its perceived importance has been enhanced by the archaeology of concurrent collapse — the exact circularity the audit smelled;

3. a paleoclimatologist's critique notes the partition lumps together droughts and wet periods sometimes centuries from 4.2 ka;

4. hemispheric asymmetry — Southern-Hemisphere proxies read wet, the lower Yangtze reads flood; no single uniform global drought;

5. the Gol-e-Zard record itself is two humps, not one instant (date-free, by depth; the authors place onsets at 4.51 ka and 4.26 ka).

Net for the cascade. "Drought" may not be used as a load-bearing counter-fact against a flood/internal/political reading — nor for it. Only R0 (an excursion exists in this one rock) is carried, as present-tense [V]; every rung from R2 up is [O] and is released to the independent geochronology/history channel where the firewall already routes occurrence and cause. This is the conservative posture the audit asked for: keep the measured rung, hold everything unproven above it. Gate: f9f192f09276fe3f6c8924fd92c0b42d1f203d746a9134224b59af7fe9ed152e. Raw file SHA-256: 86667741602354478c990fe4e1b423fccbf7f6481c8e2a78d18b15c4c35867b7.

Correction logged (mark-never-erase). Part D's prose "broadly drought in Mesopotamia and Egypt" overstated a D5/[O] interpretation as if settled.
