# Module 33 — Latitude energy-balance permission screen: the termination fork

In plain terms. The Sun does not warm the planet the same way through the year. Averaged over a year the equator gets the most light; at midsummer the pole actually gets the most (24-hour day). So when an ice age ends, which latitude melts first depends on which of those two balances controls the melt — and that is a fork in the road, not one fixed story. What we can check today is firm: the ice that exists at high latitudes is locked in by its own brightness, exactly as a bistable switch would predict.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence · glaciation-driven petroleum branch) · Inherits: Constitution Art. 1/2/4/7, the dual-redox core (overview). Firewall: present-tense observables load-bearing; absolute date/rate/occurrence [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. Insolation has two shapes — annual-mean monotonic (equator-hot) and summer-solstice pole-peaked — so the termination ordering is forced into a fork (annual control ⇒ equatorward-first; summer control ⇒ pole-weighted, the mainstream 65°N shape), and which branch controls is itself a present-tense question. Established high-latitude ice is insolation-locked (bistable) — observed now (Antarctica, Greenland). The fork, not a single sweep, is the firewall-clean structural result.

## 1. What is computed (present-tense, no chronology)

Annual-mean and summer-solstice top-of-atmosphere insolation by latitude, from the present orbit (obliquity 23.44°, eccentricity 0.0167). No past orbital variation is used — that is the firewalled pacing the mainstream relies on. A build index (warm-ocean snow engine ~ (SST−Tair)×Clausius–Clapeyron) and a melt index (absorbed insolation minus the OLR of a melting, ~273 K surface) are evaluated under two controls: annual-mean absorbed vs summer absorbed.

## 2. The fork (the new structural object)

Annual-mean insolation is monotonic (equator-hot, pole-cold); summer-solstice insolation is non-monotonic (peaks at the pole). So the termination ordering forced as the warm-ocean fuel wanes depends on which energy balance controls melt — and that is a present-tense screen, not a chronology. This branch — not a single monotonic sweep — is the firewall-clean result.

## 3. Correction carried (mark-never-erase)

An earlier form of this screen claimed ice is insolation-locked at all latitudes (a snowball lock). That all-latitude lock was a toy energy-balance artifact (uniform albedo 0.70, no heat transport); real tropical ice melts (dirty-ice albedo ~0.4–0.5 plus heat transport). It is trimmed to the observationally-true claim: the high-latitude lock we actually observe. The original wording stands with this correction appended.

# Module 38 — Cracking-clock closure: the geological rock-cycle clock binds, Gyr-retention refuted

In plain terms. People say oil can survive a billion years in a hot reservoir, so its presence proves nothing about timing. But a billion-year survival has to survive the rock cycle too — and traps and source rocks do not last that long (they get buried and turned to gas/graphite, or lifted up and eroded). So the “billion-year retention” idea is refuted by the slower of the two clocks. That said, the rock-cycle clock still allows very long times, so the absolute age stays open either way.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence · glaciation-driven petroleum branch) · Inherits: Constitution Art. 1/2/4/7, the dual-redox core (overview). Firewall: present-tense observables load-bearing; absolute date/rate/occurrence [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. Two clocks bound oil survival. The thermal cracking clock at a typical ~90 °C reservoir is loose (~Gyr); but the geological rock-cycle clock (~10⁷–10⁸ yr — burial to gas/graphite, or exhumation to erosion) binds far below it. ## 1. Two clocks, not one

Thermal clock: at ~90 °C oil→gas cracking is slow (~Gyr). Taken alone it buys no recency edge. Geological clock: the trap and the rock do not survive a Gyr — the rock cycle either buries them deeper (oil→gas→graphite) or exhumes and erodes them, on ~10⁷–10⁸ yr. The binding clock is the geological one.

## 2. The correction (mark-never-erase)

The prior turn said “oil survives deep time at ~90 °C, no problem” — a one-sided thermal-only reading. It ignored the rock cycle. The author's Persian-Gulf / Babylon objection (a thing that survives thermally must still survive the rock cycle, which it does not) is conceded. Gyr-retention is refuted; the original wording stands with this two-clock correction appended.

# Module 41 — 3D basin-geometry source model (the keystone): where the oil actually is

In plain terms. Why is oil where it is? Not simply by latitude. Thick ice piles on continents; when it melts fast, the meltwater and ground-up rock flush off the land into the next-door restricted basin — exactly where source rocks form. So the real control is how restricted the basin is, fed either by cold meltwater (high latitude) or warm seas (low latitude). The open ocean gets neither and stays barren. That is the actual map of the world's oil — North Sea, West Siberia, Persian Gulf, the Atlantic rifts — and the empty deep ocean.

So the axis is basin geometry (restriction) + meltwater routing, not zonal climate.

## 2. Two routes to an anoxic, productive basin (both gated by restriction)

(A) High-latitude meltwater route: thick continental ice melts → freshwater lid + glacial-flour nutrients flush into the down-slope basin → stratified, fertilised. (B) Low-latitude warm route: warm event ocean + tropical productivity in a restricted/evaporitic basin → stratified, fertilised. Open ocean gets neither restriction nor a lid → well-mixed, oxygenated → barren.

## 3. It matches the real map

The favourability field peaks in restricted basins downstream of continental ice and in warm restricted seas, and is barren in the open ocean — exactly the observed distribution (North Sea, West Siberia, Persian Gulf, the Atlantic conjugate rifts) and the deep-ocean void. The cascade predicts the geography of oil.

# Module 42 — Oil quality from the glaciation cascade: the dual-redox fingerprint (6/6)

In plain terms. The same meltwater that makes oil's source rock also sets the oil's quality — by doing opposite things at two depths. Deep down it seals off oxygen, preserving the organic source. Up shallow, cold oxygen-bearing meltwater seeps into the reservoir and lets microbes eat the light parts of the oil, leaving it heavy. So Athabasca's tar sands (cold, shallow, meltwater-flushed) are extra-heavy, while the North Sea (deep, hot) is light — and the model recovers all six real provinces from their settings alone.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence · glaciation-driven petroleum branch) · Inherits: Constitution Art. 1/2/4/7, the dual-redox core (overview). Firewall: present-tense observables load-bearing; absolute date/rate/occurrence [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. If the cascade controls the environment, it should control the oil quality too. The driver is the glaciation: meltwater plays a dual redox role — at the deep source a freshwater lid sequesters oxygen (anoxia → good source rock); at the shallow reservoir cool oxygen-bearing recharge does the reverse (biodegradation → heavy oil). From three present-tense knobs (reservoir temperature, meltwater recharge, sulfur potential) the model recovers 6/6 provinces' heavy/light + sour/sweet class: Athabasca extra-heavy, North Sea light, Arabian sour, West Siberia light, Orinoco extra-heavy, Monterey heavy-sour.

## 1. The dual-redox mechanism

One oxygen knob, two depths, opposite outcomes. Deep source: meltwater lid sequesters O₂ → anoxia → organic preservation → good source rock. Shallow reservoir: cool, oxygen/nutrient-bearing meltwater recharge → microbes biodegrade the oil (eat the light ends) → heavy oil. Biodegradation shuts off above ~80 °C (microbes die), so deep/hot reservoirs stay light.

## 2. Three present-tense knobs → quality

From repro/data/oil_quality_provinces.csv: reservoir temperature (depth: hot/deep → lighter, and biodegradation off), meltwater recharge × cool reservoir → biodegradation → heavier, and sulfur potential (evaporite-sulfate or Type II-S) → sour. The model predicts each province's class and compares to the observed quality.

## 3. The result — 6/6

Athabasca (57°N, cool, meltwater-flushed, shallow) → extra-heavy; North Sea (58°N but deep, hot) → light sweet — latitude alone does not set quality; depth/temp + recharge do. Arabian carbonate+anhydrite → sour; Monterey Type II-S → heavy sour. 6/6 provinces recovered from environment alone.

Environment (reservoir T, recharge setting, evaporite) and oil quality present-tense [V]; quality-from-environment a constructed forward model that recovers the observed pattern. Timing/occurrence [O], untouched.

# Module 44 — Deglaciation recency from ongoing rebound (present-tense): corrects M35

In plain terms. Hudson Bay and Scandinavia are still rising today — the ground is springing back after heavy ice was removed. A springy-but-slow mantle relaxes over thousands of years; if the ice had gone hundreds of millions of years ago, the land would already sit flat with no rise left. The fact that it is rising now means the ice melted recently, on the order of ten thousand years. This needs no calendar date and no assumed decay rate — just the springback we measure today. It is a present-tense fact about the ice, not a claim that the flood is proven recent.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence · glaciation-driven petroleum branch) · Inherits: Constitution Art. 1/2/4/7, the dual-redox core (overview). Firewall: present-tense observables load-bearing; absolute date/rate/occurrence [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. The rebound is still going in the old ice centres (~1 cm/yr today). With the present mantle relaxation time τ (from the measured viscosity), ongoing uplift is only possible if unloading was within ~1–2 τ, i.e. order 10⁴ yr ago; were it 10⁸ yr ago (~10⁴ τ), the remaining uplift would be ~exp(−25000) ≈ 0 — flat, no uplift. So the deglaciation's recency is present-tense [V], from ongoing springback, no calendar date and no assumed rate. This corrects M35's over-firewalling of timing.

## 1. The physics (present-tense)

A viscous mantle under a removed load relaxes with a characteristic time τ = 4πη/(ρgλ) (fundamental mode, load wavelength λ). After time t since unloading the remaining uplift decays as exp(−t/τ). If t ~ a few τ, uplift is still going; if t » τ (e.g. 10⁸ yr = thousands of τ), it is complete. We measure ~1 cm/yr of uplift today in the old ice centres → unloading was within ~1–2 τ.

## 2. The verdict

Rebound is still going, so with τ of order 10⁴ yr the deglaciation was recent, order 10⁴ yr. This is exactly the author's “last ice age” logic, and it needs no calendar date and no assumed decay rate — just the ongoing springback we measure now. [V].

## 3. Correction to M35, and the firewall boundary (mark-never-erase)

Module 35 hid deglaciation timing behind a symbol ([O] both ways). That was over-firewalling: the qualitative fact that rebound is ongoing is present-tense and forces a recency bound. Crucial boundary: this is a present-tense observable about the ice, not a past-occurrence claim — the cascade's occurrence stays [O] (the flood/coupling absolute timing is not promoted). Only the precise calendar number keeps mild viscosity-model dependence.

## 4. Consequence for the cascade

The ice event is provably recent, so “when did the ice melt” is settled (recent), not an open mystery. The only timing question left is whether the source/salt/rift belong to this same recent relaxation — the coupling question (the single open frontier; see overview and Module 45).

## 2. The relaxation-tail degeneracy (the firewall, made rigorous [F])

Maxwell time τ = η/μ ≈ 488 yr (solid on seismic seconds → S-waves; fluid on Myr → convects); the inherited rupture engine moves by stick-slip (duty cycle ~1.3×10⁻⁹: apparent slow rate = sparse fast slip). Then the core result: given only a present rate vnow and a decaying history v(t)=v₀exp(−t/T), the relation vnow=v₀exp(−tnow/T) is one equation in two unknowns → a one-parameter family for every T. A single present-rate measurement is informationally insufficient to date the event: “slow now” fits both slow-old and recent-fast-with-tail. Present rate [V]; inferred age [O] both ways. This defends the two-edged firewall — it does not smuggle “recent.”

## 3. One-substrate consistency with M44 (present-tense [V] / age [O])

The same mantle viscosity (η = 10²¹) sets two relaxation modes of the same jammed solid: M44's flexural (load) τ ≈ 4100 yr and the Maxwell (shear) τ ≈ 488 yr. Honest asymmetry: M44 earns recency for the ice from an observed incompleteness (rebound is still going); spreading has no such present-tense incompleteness datum here, so its absolute age stays [O]. The import gives a causal frame (one jammed substrate, one forced cell), not a date for the rift.

## 4. What this gives the cascade (graded honestly [L])

# Module 46 — Magnitude-ratio discriminator (SH-26): the one genuinely-discriminating test, built and run

In plain terms. If one event really set the whole oil suite, then the ratios between its parts (salt vs stretch, source vs stretch, salt vs source) should be the same everywhere — a fixed recipe. If instead each part has its own cause (the mainstream view), those ratios should vary from place to place. Salt-vs-stretch is tied together in both pictures, so it can't decide. The deciding ratios — source-vs-stretch and salt-vs-source — come out in between: not fixed enough to prove one event, not varied enough to prove separate causes. So even this last test can't cleanly tell the two apart.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence · glaciation-driven petroleum branch). Builds the SH-26 test named by M39. Firewall: present-tense geometry/richness load-bearing; absolute date/rate/occurrence [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. A one-parameter relaxation predicts the petroleum-suite magnitude ratios are universal constants (tight scatter); the mainstream predicts the cross-control ratios (source/extension, salt/source) scatter (independent climate vs productivity controls). Run on the South Atlantic segments with pre-registered thresholds: salt/extension is tight but degenerate (mechanical, both frameworks); the two cross-control ratios are intermediate (CV 0.18–0.19) ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE. SH-26 thus joins basal-character (M37) and P5 co-variation (M39) as a third present-tense axis that is degenerate between the frameworks; the decisive across-independent-systems version stays [O]/unbuilt (it needs verified volumes, not guessed ones).

## 1. Why this module exists

Module 39 ended by naming the only test that could separate the cascade from the mainstream past the rate firewall: a genuinely discriminating version would need a magnitude RATIO the one-parameter budget predicts and independent-magnitude mainstream does not (the open C-2 candidate, SH-26) — still UNBUILT. This module builds it and runs it on the only internally-consistent frozen present-tense dataset available (the South Atlantic conjugate-margin segments, M39's data).

## 2. Why this is NOT the degenerate M39 co-variation

A single conserved relaxation (one parameter) would set the whole suite, so all pairwise magnitude ratios should be universal constants — low scatter. The mainstream treats the magnitudes as independent: salt is set by accommodation + restriction + arid climate; the source rock by productivity + anoxia. Different controls ⇒ the cross-control ratios should scatter.

Crucially, salt/extension is mechanical (more stretch → more accommodation → more salt) in both frameworks, so it is degenerate — M39 already showed it co-varies (r = +0.99). It is reported but is not the discriminator. The discriminator is the cross-control ratios source/extension and salt/source: tight ⇒ one-parameter; scattered ⇒ mainstream.

## 3. The result (honest, pre-registered thresholds)

Thresholds declared before reading the data (not fitted): CV < 0.15 tight; CV > 0.35 scattered; between = intermediate. Across the six segments:

| Ratio | role | CV | reading

| salt / extension | mechanical — degenerate | 0.036 | tight (both frameworks; not discriminating)

| source(TOC) / extension | cross-control | 0.175 | intermediate

| salt / source(TOC) | cross-control | 0.193 | intermediate

Verdict: INCONCLUSIVE. The two cross-control ratios land in the intermediate band — neither tight enough to confirm a one-parameter universal constant, nor scattered enough to confirm independent mainstream magnitudes. The test does not cleanly discriminate.

## 4. Honest caveats (load-bearing on the grade)

Three limits are stated up front, not after the result. (1) All six segments are one rift system (the South Atlantic opening), not independent realisations of different coupled events; a within-system ratio cannot be a universal-constant test. (2) Source magnitude is proxied by TOC (richness), not volume (thickness×area) — the frozen set has no source thickness, and the TOC column is coarse (three buckets). (3) n = 6.

## 5. The decisive version (specified, and why it stays [O]/unbuilt)

The decisive test is the same ratio across independent salt-giant systems — South Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico, Red Sea, Zechstein, Messinian, Pricaspian (the canonical population, so no cherry-picking) — with verified source-rock volumes. If the cross-control ratio is the same across these independent systems ⇒ a universal constant (strong one-parameter); if it varies by system ⇒ local control (mainstream). This run is UNRUN: it needs verified cross-system volumes, and fabricating those numbers would violate the framework (no unverified data, no fitting), so it is left [O]/unbuilt rather than guessed.

## 6. Grade and what it means for the cascade

The SH-26 discriminator is now built and specified, not merely named. The within-system run is [L]/inconclusive: salt/extension tight (degenerate), cross-control ratios intermediate. So SH-26 joins M37 (basal-character) and M39 (P5 co-variation) as a third present-tense axis that is degenerate between the frameworks. The honest standing is unchanged and now triply-demonstrated: no present-tense observable cleanly separates the cascade from the mainstream; the framework's edge remains coherence and parsimony, and absolute timing / occurrence stay [O], both directions. Falsification = discovery.

the better bet. That economy — closing the whole thing causally, without tuning — is the real value.

# Module 48 — Causal-ordering / superposition test (SH-66): the SYNTHESIS "#1 build", built and run

In plain terms. You can't read the dates off the rocks without breaking the firewall — but you can read the order: which layer sits on top of which is a fact you see today. The cascade predicts a specific stacking order — the basin forms, then the source rock is laid down, then oil rises into the rock above it; and where there was ice, the glacial layer sits below the source rock. Across eight major oil basins that order holds every time (16 out of 16 checks). That's a real pass — if it had failed, the story would break. But here's the honest catch: the ordinary textbook account predicts the same order (you must bury a source rock before its oil can rise), so passing doesn't prove this story over that one. And the one place the strong version of the claim could have won — salt always in the same spot — fails: salt sits above the source in the Atlantic pre-salt but below it in the North Sea and Gulf of Mexico. So the order is real and consistent, but it can't tell the two frameworks apart.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: 1 (Recent-Sequence · glaciation-driven petroleum branch). Builds the test named by SYNTHESIS Task A. Firewall: present-tense superposition (ordinal stacking) load-bearing; absolute date/rate/occurrence [O]/RECORD, both directions.

One line. The SYNTHESIS document named stratigraphic superposition the single most important remaining build (order is present-tense; dates are not). Built and run on eight giant-oil basins: the cascade's three causally-forced relations — rift < source, glacial < source, source < oil — are concordant 16/16 [V], so the chain order is internally consistent and is not broken. But those same relations are forced by ordinary basin evolution in the mainstream too (deposition→burial→migration; post-glacial anoxia is textbook), so the concordance is non-discriminating; and the strong "one fixed coupled order" reading is REFUTED — salt sits above source in the South Atlantic pre-salt but below it in the North Sea and Gulf of Mexico (non-universal). Superposition thus joins M34/M35/M37/M39/M46 as a degenerate present-tense axis, confirming Module 20 / Module 47 — and the SYNTHESIS hope that order would be the decisive build is itself honestly corrected. Coupling-as-one-event and absolute timing stay [O], both directions.

## 1. Why this module exists

The SYNTHESIS & Remaining Tasks document was explicit: the firewall caps absolute dates but NOT stratigraphic superposition — relative order is present-tense ... this is the single most important remaining build. It is firewall-clean precisely because order is not a date: which unit sits below which is a fact one reads today, with no chronology imported. This module builds that test and runs it, so the program's own highest-priority item is no longer merely named.

## 2. The predicted order and the three forced relations

One coupled relaxation predicts a deposition order (deepest/earliest → shallowest/latest):

RIFT < GLACIAL < SOURCE < SALT < RES_OIL

Three of these relations are causally necessary — if the chain is real they must hold, and if they were violated basin-to-basin the chain would break:

| relation | why it is causally forced

| RIFT < SOURCE | the basin must exist before it can be filled with an organic-rich bed

| GLACIAL < SOURCE | the post-glacial meltwater lid → stratification → anoxia produces the source bed, so the glacial unit sits below it

| SOURCE < RES_OIL | oil migrates upward only after the source rock is buried and matured

The FLOOD stage is deliberately excluded: calling a particular clastic unit a "flood deposit" is an interpretation, and importing it would contaminate a present-tense test. Only non-interpretive lithostratigraphic units (rift, glaciogenic diamictite, source shale, evaporite, reservoir) are used.

## 3. The result (honest, pre-registered rule)

Decision rule declared before reading the data (not fitted): core relations are ORDER-CONSISTENT if concordance ≥ 0.90; the salt position is universal only if every basin carrying both salt and source agrees in sign. Eight giant-oil basins (South Atlantic pre-salt ×3, North Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and three Palaeozoic glaciogenic systems in North Africa / Arabia):

| core relation | concordant basins | reading

| RIFT < SOURCE | 5 / 5 | holds

| GLACIAL < SOURCE | 3 / 3 | holds (post-glacial hot-shale sources)

| SOURCE < RES_OIL | 8 / 8 | holds (upward migration)

| CORE CONCORDANCE | 16 / 16 = 1.000 | ORDER-CONSISTENT [V]

The chain's predicted order is not violated anywhere — a genuine pass of a test that could have failed.

## 4. The strong reading, tested — and refuted

If a single fixed coupled order were imprinted by one event, salt would sit in a universal position relative to the source rock. It does not:

| basin | salt vs source

| Santos / Campos / Kwanza (South Atlantic pre-salt) | salt ABOVE source

| Central Graben (North Sea, Zechstein) | salt BELOW source

| Gulf of Mexico (Louann) | salt BELOW source

Salt position is NON-UNIVERSAL (above in 3, below in 2). The strong "one fixed coupled order" reading is therefore REFUTED [V]. Salt position is set by local setting — sag-phase evaporite capping a lacustrine source in the pre-salt, versus early-rift/drift evaporite beneath a later marine source elsewhere — which both frameworks accommodate. Falsification = discovery.

## 5. Discrimination verdict

The concordance is real and present-tense [V], but it is not a discriminator: the same three relations are forced by ordinary mainstream basin evolution (deposition→burial→migration; post-glacial transgressive anoxia is the textbook origin of the Silurian hot-shale source rocks themselves). And the one reading that could have separated the frameworks — a universal salt position — is refuted. So superposition joins basal-character (M37), GIA geometry (M35), deglacial pattern (M34), P5 co-variation (M39) and the magnitude ratio (M46) as a degenerate present-tense axis. This is exactly the structural prediction of Module 20 and the reason Module 47 moves the value criterion off single discriminators and onto tuning-free causal closure.

## 6. Grade and what it means for the cascade

SH-66 is now built and run, not merely named. The causal order is present-tense consistent [V] (the chain is not broken); the strong fixed-order over-reading is refuted [V]; the test is non-discriminating between the frameworks. The honest consequence is twofold: the cascade survives a test that could have falsified it, and the SYNTHESIS document's hope that superposition would be the decisive build is itself corrected — order constrains, but it does not decide. Whether these phenomena are causally one event, and all absolute timing, stay [O], both directions. Falsification = discovery.

# Module 50 — SH-5 reservoir-budget bound: the dominant [O] root, bounded present-tense

In plain terms. The whole chain has always leaned on one demanding question: is there enough deep water for the flood and the ice? This module answers the part you can answer today. Diamonds bring up a mineral (ringwoodite) that is about 1.4% water by weight, and estimates put the water stored deep inside the Earth at roughly one to two oceans' worth. That is about ten times more than even the largest amount the chain needs. So "is there enough water down there?" is no longer the sticking point — there is. What stays genuinely open is a different question: how much of that buried water could actually be released to the surface in one event, and by what mechanism. That part has no present-day measurement, so it stays open. The bottleneck didn't vanish — it got smaller and more precise.

SH-5 moves from unbounded bottleneck to inventory ample, release fraction unknown.

# Module 52 — Tier-4 mainstream stress-test: every load-bearing claim against the strongest objection

In plain terms. This is the test the author always planned to run last: deliberately turn the strongest mainstream geology against the theory and see what breaks. For each of the theory's fifteen load-bearing claims, the page states the best version of the mainstream's counter-argument — not a weak caricature — and then judges honestly who wins. The verdict is sobering and clean: the theory is not refuted (it never claimed the events happened), but under maximum pressure it wins nothing on present-tense grounds — every distinctive test turns out to be a tie with the mainstream, and the one place the theory is genuinely exposed is a single step: whether the deep-water reservoir can actually be released. The whole risk of the framework sits on that one step. That honest result is the point.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Exposed to the strongest steelmanned mainstream objections, the cascade survives as a physically-permitted, internally-coherent construction but gains ZERO present-tense discriminating advantage: of 15 load-bearing claims, 7 are [V]-but-degenerate (the mainstream predicts the same), 3 survive as [L] coherence only, 3 concede a load-bearing step — and all three trace to ONE root, the S0 reservoir release (SH-5) — and 2 stay open. ## 1. The rules of this stress-test

Three commitments make this an honest adversarial test rather than a defence:

(a) Steelman, not strawman. Each mainstream objection is stated as its real positive case — the mechanism the mainstream actually offers, with its own evidence — not a weak caricature that is easy to dismiss. The constitution requires it: a favoured and a disfavoured interpretation of the same observation receive the same grade (GOVERNANCE, audit principle).

(b) The firewall cuts both ways. Where a mainstream objection rests on absolute chronology — "spreading took ~180 Myr", the radiometric calibration of magnetic stripes — that chronological form is [O] in both directions and is not counted against the cascade. Only the firewall-clean, present-tense content of each objection is adjudicated. Equally, the cascade may not promote occurrence; it stays [O].

(c) A refutation is a finding. The aim is not to make the cascade win. If a load-bearing step concedes, that is recorded as a result and localised, not explained away. The single most valuable output of this module is knowing exactly where the framework is most exposed.

## 2. The mainstream's strongest mechanisms (steelmanned)

The objections draw on the mainstream's best-evidenced machinery, each independently supported in the present-tense record:

| domain | the mainstream mechanism (its real positive case)

| glaciation | Milankovitch orbital insolation + ice-albedo/CO₂ feedbacks; ice-sheet hysteresis and threshold termination (Abe-Ouchi-type)

| ocean opening | ridge-push + slab-pull + mantle convection; present-tense symmetric magnetic-anomaly stripes (Vine-Matthews), age-distance, GPS plate motion

| source rock | oceanic anoxic events (Schlanger-Jenkyns): warm climate + sluggish circulation + productivity over extended intervals

| crustal faulting | glacial-isostatic adjustment drives shallow intraplate seismicity (Fennoscandian postglacial faults ~M6-7) — but does not open basins

| petroleum | the standard petroleum system (Magoon-Dow): source-reservoir-seal-trap-timing, basin by basin

| evaporites | extension → accommodation + restriction → evaporite volume (basic basin mechanics)

These are not free parameters; each carries its own evidence. That fact is the heart of the objection to the 8:1 value claim (C14 below).

## 3. The adjudication (15 load-bearing claims)

The full reasoning for each row is frozen in repro/data/tier4_stress_ledger.csv and tallied deterministically by the script. Verdicts: DEGENERATE (survives present-tense but the mainstream predicts the same — no advantage); CONCEDE (the mainstream wins a load-bearing step; the cascade holds it [O]); COHERENCE-ONLY (survives as [L] internal consistency, not evidence); OPEN / OPEN-BY-DESIGN (decisive test unbuilt, or firewalled).

## 4. What the tally shows

The deterministic counts: 7 DEGENERATE, 3 CONCEDE, 3 COHERENCE-ONLY, 1 OPEN, 1 OPEN-BY-DESIGN. Two facts matter most.

The central invariant — zero wins. Not one distinctive claim emerges with a discriminating present-tense advantage over the mainstream. Every axis the cascade might have won on (the petroleum-geography keystone M41, the salt-extension covariation M39, the superposition order M48, the source-rock facies M37, the forebulge geometry M35) is degenerate — the mainstream predicts the same present-tense result. This is the Module 20 structural-degeneracy finding, now confirmed against the mainstream's explicit best mechanisms rather than asserted. The script asserts this invariant (no DISCRIMINATING_WIN verdict exists) and fails if it is ever violated.

The concentrated point of failure — one root. The mainstream holds this implausible on flood timescales; the cascade holds it [O]. The framework's entire empirical risk is concentrated here — exactly what the weak-link audit (M29) and the reservoir-budget bound (M50) already located, now confirmed under adversarial pressure. The script asserts that every conceded step belongs to this root.

## 5. The verdict on the 8:1 value claim (C14)

The capstone (M47) rests the framework's value on an 8:1 causal compression: one untuned cause closing nine phenomena where the mainstream uses eight independent mechanisms. The strongest mainstream rebuttal lands: those eight mechanisms are each independently evidenced (orbital forcing, plate tectonics, oceanic anoxic events, glacial-isostatic adjustment, the petroleum system each carry their own present-tense support), so they are not free parameters; and the cascade's single cause rests on one enormous open assumption — the S0 release. The honest restatement: the cascade trades eight independently-evidenced mechanisms for one mechanism plus one enormous [O] release, and that release does the work the eight do while lacking their evidence. The 8:1 is a real compression in mechanism-count and fitted-parameter-count (zero tuned vs many), and it is defensible as an [L] aesthetic preference — but it is not an epistemic advantage, and a rigorous mainstream reviewer is entitled to decline it. The v30 capstone tightening already states this (risk concentrated in SH-5); the stress-test confirms it.

## 6. What the stress-test does — and does not — establish

It does not refute the cascade. The framework never claimed occurrence; an honest tie on present-tense discriminators and a single [O] load-bearing step are exactly the standing it has always declared. Nor does it vindicate the mainstream's deep-time reading: that reading is also not forced by the firewall-clean present-tense data alone — the same degeneracy cuts both ways. What it establishes is a clean, externally-audited map of the terrain: the cascade is permitted and coherent, wins nothing present-tense, and is exposed at precisely one point. That is the most useful thing an adversarial test can produce, and it is recorded without flinching. Falsification = discovery.

## Reproducibility

The consuming script (repro/m52_tier4_mainstream_stress_test.py) pins the frozen adjudication ledger by raw SHA-256, validates every verdict, asserts the central invariant (no discriminating-win verdict) and the concentrated-root invariant (every conceded step belongs to the S0-release root), prints the tally and bottom line, and proves determinism with a double-SHA-256 self-gate. SEED = 19, no fitted parameter. The ledger is an explicit reasoning artifact; readers are invited to contest any row — that is the design.

2×SHA-256 (ledger body) = 666f617cd822fb8194b0d5a93ec37cf2825dc51edcf3d2b96922d7a4e53e4bb4

python3 repro/m52_tier4_mainstream_stress_test.py → prints the adjudication, recomputes the hash, asserts equality (REPRO GATE: PASS).

Module 52 complete. The author-planned Tier-4 adversarial phase is run: 15 load-bearing claims exposed to the strongest steelmanned mainstream mechanisms, adjudicated under the firewall. The cascade survives as a permitted, coherent construction with zero present-tense discriminating advantage (7 degenerate, 3 coherence-only, 3 conceding at the single S0-release root, 2 open); the 8:1 value claim is [L] elegance, not epistemic advantage; occurrence stays [O], both directions. No occurrence was promoted; the single greatest vulnerability is localised to SH-5. Falsification = discovery.

# Module 53 — Ordering-seam discharge (B.5 / T3.2): the last author-held item, verified

In plain terms. Earlier, the theory's two halves were shown to fit on one timeline — the ice builds and triggers the rupture first, the inherited "what happens when an ocean opens" physics comes after — but only if none of that later physics secretly assumed there was no ice beforehand. That "if" was written down and left to be checked. This module does the check, going through all eight inherited after-the-opening mechanisms one by one. None of them need an ice-free start; in fact one of them (oil formation) positively needs the ice, because the oil source rock is made by glacial meltwater. So the "if" is satisfied, and the two halves join into one timeline for good. This is a tidy internal-consistency result — it does not claim the events happened; the genuinely open questions stay open.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: internal-consistency closure (roadmap T3.2, Blueprint B.5). Discharges: the deferred condition of Module 30 (SH-41). Firewall: present-tense mechanism only; occurrence/timing [O] both directions.

One line. M30 closed the ordering seam conditionally — one timeline (glaciation pre-rupture, inherited responses post-rupture) provided no inherited post-opening response presupposes an ice-free pre-rupture state — and deferred the check. This module runs it against all eight inherited responses of the parent volume: zero conflicts; one response is actively reinforced (petroleum needs the glacial meltwater, so an ice-free pre-state would break it). The condition is therefore met, and SH-41 is promoted from [F]-conditional to [F]; the seam closes unconditionally. The trigger near-criticality (SH-40), the S0 release (SH-5), and occurrence stay [O], both directions. Falsification = discovery.

## 1. The deferred check, stated exactly

Module 30 resolved the ordering seam to one timeline and named the single condition under which it holds (SH-41):

Consistency condition. No inherited post-opening response may presuppose an ice-free pre-rupture state. None is apparent (the opening dynamics, the thermal relaxation, and petroleum formation do not require the prior absence of ice). This should be verified against the inherited volume's content; if any response is found to require an ice-free pre-state, the conflict is real and the honest fix is to revise the pre-loading magnitude — not to ignore the conflict (Art. 7).

M30 stated the condition and the failure branch but deferred the verification itself. That verification is the author-held item (roadmap T3.2 / Blueprint B.5). This module performs it — not by re-declaring consistency, but by adjudicating each inherited response against the ice-free question, with the failure branch pre-registered.

## 2. The pre-registered rule

Declared before adjudication (and frozen in the ledger): the ordering condition is DISCHARGED iff the CONFLICT count is exactly 0. A response is graded CONFLICT only if its mechanism requires the pre-rupture crust to be ice-free; any such finding keeps the seam open and routes to the Art. 7 revision branch (revise the pre-loading magnitude — never ignore the conflict). A response that does not presuppose ice-free is CONSISTENT; one that positively requires the ice (so an ice-free pre-state would break it) is REINFORCED. The firewall holds: the question is strictly about ice-free presupposition, a present-tense mechanism property — not about when anything happened.

## 3. The eight inherited post-opening responses, adjudicated

The inherited responses are taken from the parent Atlantic-Expansion volume as inherited and confirmed in Module 21 (all eight referenced quantities verified there, bundle re-run 39/39). The full reasoning per row is frozen in repro/data/orderseam_iceFree_ledger.csv.

| id | inherited post-opening response | requires ice-free pre-state? | verdict

| R1 | Void-suction acceleration engine (deep pressure-deficit void drives sliding) | No — powered by deep ΔP, indifferent to surface ice | CONSISTENT

| R2 | Unjamming / liquefaction friction collapse (State 4→3, no melt) | No — driven by slip shear-heating, not surface conditions | CONSISTENT

| R3 | Stick-slip spreading / duty-cycle opening kinematics | No — a basal-friction bistability of the gouge; surface ice does not enter | CONSISTENT

| R4 | Re-jamming thermal self-limit (τ = h²/κ ≈ 9 s) | No — a diffusive shear-band timescale, internal | CONSISTENT

| R5 | Energy budget of the opening (W_in = ΔP·A_eff·d ≈ 3×10²⁶ J) | No — derives from ΔP, void area, displacement; no surface-ice term | CONSISTENT

| R6 | Cold-thick-lithosphere siting (parent's independent prediction) | No — about lithospheric thermal structure; a cold surface is compatible, not excluded | CONSISTENT

| R7 | Post-opening thermal relaxation (lithospheric cooling / subsidence) | No — driven by the margin's decaying heat structure | CONSISTENT

| R8 | Petroleum formation in the opened basins (source → burial + heat → oil) | No — and the opposite: the source rock needs the glacial meltwater lid | REINFORCED

## 4. The result

The deterministic tally: 7 CONSISTENT, 1 REINFORCED, 0 CONFLICT. By the pre-registered rule, zero conflicts means the condition is DISCHARGED. Two things are worth stating precisely:

The condition is met, not merely assumed. Every inherited post-opening mechanism — the suction engine, the unjamming friction collapse, the stick-slip kinematics, the re-jamming self-limit, the energy budget, the cold-thick siting, the thermal relaxation — operates on deep or thermal variables that do not reference whether ice sat on the surface beforehand. None requires an ice-free pre-state, so none competes with the cascade's pre-rupture glaciation. The one-timeline reading holds unconditionally.

One response is reinforced. Petroleum formation (R8) is stronger than consistent: the cascade's source rock is made by meltwater-lid stratification → anoxia → organic burial (M37/M41), which positively requires the glacial meltwater. An ice-free pre-state would remove the meltwater lid and break the source-rock mechanism — the strict opposite of presupposing ice-free. So the inherited petroleum response does not merely tolerate the glacial pre-state; it depends on it.

## 5. Grade and residue

SH-41 is promoted from [F] conditional to [F] discharged: the condition has been verified against the inherited volume's content, response by response, with the failure branch pre-registered and not triggered. The B.5 ordering seam — the last author-held item — is now closed unconditionally, and the chain's internal-consistency requirement is fully met (acyclic per M29; single-valued trigger and one timeline per M30; condition discharged here).

The residue is named and unchanged. This closes an internal-consistency seam only; it promotes nothing about occurrence. The trigger near-criticality (SH-40), the S0 reservoir release (SH-5, the framework's concentrated vulnerability per M52), and all absolute timing / occurrence stay [O], both directions. The loading-vs-unloading direction of the trigger is the separate trigger seam (M30 §1, SH-39/40), not this ordering check. Falsification = discovery.

## Reproducibility

The consuming script (repro/m53_ordering_seam_discharge.py) pins the frozen ledger by raw SHA-256, validates each verdict (and the internal rule that only an ice-free-requiring response may be a CONFLICT), applies the pre-registered decision (discharge iff CONFLICTs = 0), prints the adjudication and the discharge, and proves determinism with a double-SHA-256 self-gate. SEED = 19, no fitted parameter, no new physics, no dates.

## PART 5 — WHAT STAYS [O] FOREVER, AND THE STANDING FALSIFIER

- Occurrence is capped. No accumulation of Tier-A observation promotes any historical-occurrence claim above [O] (Constitution Art. 4.2). The chain's physical permission is what advances; its happening is not provable and is not claimed.

- The standing external falsifier is declared, not hidden (Constitution Art. 1.4). Independent chronometers (igneous U–Pb on baddeleyite/zircon; reservoir-free, historically-anchored radiocarbon) press on the recency reading (H-R) and are treated as a permanent open item. The framework does not assert them wrong; it holds absolute age out of arithmetic in both directions.

- The decisive empirical test is still the petroleum basal character (task A) — a depth-structure observation, not a map. It currently leans unfavourable to the glacial-transport reading (laminated marine shale, not chaotic till), with age held [O]. That honest tension is kept on the table.

# Glaciation-Driven Petroleum — overview and scorecard

In plain terms. One idea ties this whole branch together: the meltwater from a glaciation does two opposite things at two depths. Deep down it seals off oxygen and preserves the organic matter that becomes oil's source rock; up shallow it carries oxygen in and lets microbes turn the oil heavy. That single idea predicts both where the world's oil is and what kind it is — and eight independent present-day checks all line up with it.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

This page is the strand's single source of truth for the organizing mechanism and the scorecard. The modules below carry the method, the data, and the reproducibility gates.

One line. The cascade is a theory of causal coupling, not dating, driven by the glaciation (the flood is secondary). Its synthetic core is the dual-redox role of glacial meltwater; eight independent present-tense fingerprints converge on it; the carbon budget closes; the ice event is present-tense recent (M44); and the single open frontier is whether the source/salt/rift are causally part of that same recent relaxation.

The value criterion (read this): the past cannot be settled by any single present-tense discriminator — the firewall holds occurrence [O], and M37, M39 and M46 each came back degenerate. That is correct epistemics, not a weakness.

What actually distinguishes the frameworks: integrative, tuning-free causal closure. One conserved relaxation governed by the kernel closes nine present-tense phenomena with zero data-fitted parameters (a verifiable no-tuning gate), where the mainstream needs eight independent mechanisms — an 8:1 causal compression. See Module 47 (capstone).

Grade: causal closure is [L] (parsimony, not proof; occurrence stays [O]). When both frameworks fit the present and no discriminator separates them, the one untuned cause is the rational choice. Causality is the highest available value.

## 1. The synthetic core — the dual-redox role of glacial meltwater

The same water does opposite things at two depths. At the deep source it forms a freshwater lid that sequesters oxygen → anoxia → organic preservation → source rock. At the shallow reservoir, cool oxygen-bearing meltwater recharge does the reverse → biodegradation → heavy oil. One agent, one redox knob, two outcomes — and that single idea organizes both where oil is (M41) and what kind it is (M42).

## 2. The honest scorecard — eight present-tense fingerprints

Eight independent present-tense fingerprints, each of which could have failed and did not:

| # | Fingerprint | Module | Result

| 1 | substrate is bistable — high-latitude ice insolation-locked (observed) | M33 | ✓ [V]

| 2 | oil GEOGRAPHY — restricted basins downstream of ice + warm restricted seas; open ocean barren | M41 | ✓ matches the real map

| 3 | oil QUALITY — heavy/light + sour/sweet from environment | M42 | ✓ 6/6 provinces

| 4 | CARBON budget — source carbon suffices for giant oil-in-place | M43 | ✓ closes (order-of-mag)

| 5 | SALT ∝ extension along a margin | M39 | ✓ r≈+0.99

| 6 | FOREBULGE / marine-limit geometry = elastic ice-load signature | M35 | ✓ [V]

| 7 | source FACIES — quiet anoxic (the meltwater-lid basin) | M37 | ✓ [V]

| 8 | oil METASTABILITY — survives geologically (rock-cycle bound) | M38 | ✓ [V]

Plus the timing result: the ice event is present-tense recent (order 10⁴ yr, M44). The convergence of eight independent fits is the earned result; no single one is a knockout, but coincidence across all eight is increasingly implausible.

The framework’s last-named present-tense discriminator has now also been built and run: Module 46 (SH-26) tests whether the suite’s magnitude ratios are universal constants (one-parameter) or scatter (independent mainstream). On the South Atlantic data the cross-control ratios are intermediate — inconclusive. So no present-tense observable cleanly separates the cascade from the mainstream (M37, M39, M46 agree); the edge remains coherence and parsimony, and occurrence stays [O].

## 3. The five petroleum sub-questions — final standing

| Sub-question | Standing

| WHERE (geography) | solved (M41, matches data)

| QUALITY (heavy/light, sour/sweet) | solved (M42, 6/6)

| ONE EVENT (coupling) | strongly corroborated (8-fold + carbon closure); not uniquely proven

| WHEN — ice event | present-tense recent ~10⁴ yr (M44)

| WHEN — source/salt/rift absolute | [O] by design (= the coupling question)

| UNIQUENESS vs deep-time mainstream | open — non-discriminating on present-tense axes; edge = coherence/parsimony

## 4. The single open frontier (the only genuine remaining task)

One real, physical, unresolved question remains: are the source rocks, salt, and rifting causally part of the same recent relaxation as the (provably recent) deglaciation — or coincidentally a separate deep-time history?

A single metastable relaxation has one timescale: fast onset, slow-decaying tail — exactly what the ongoing rebound proves for the ice (M44). By the same logic, present-day slow rates (Atlantic spreading ~2 cm/yr) could be the decaying tail of a recent fast event rather than evidence of a slow, old process — “slow now” ≠ “slow always + old.” Module 45 imports the Continental-Genesis conservation identity, jammed-Maxwell substrate, and forced-convection loop to turn this into a causal frame and a rigorous two-edged-firewall result — without proving occurrence or recency. The genuine residual: a spreading-incompleteness datum analogous to M44's ongoing rebound. Reserved for the author's insight.

## 5. Corrections carried on the record (mark-never-erase)

This strand includes a self-audit in which the assistant found and removed its own firewall violations. The corrections preserved: M34 prior refutation retracted (firewalled antiphase); M37 prior refutation retracted (strawman + rate-claim); M38 “Gyr-retention fine” retracted (rock-cycle clock added); M33 all-latitude lock trimmed to the observed high-latitude lock; M35 over-firewalled timing, corrected by M44; M36 ×2 enrichment retracted to ~1.0–1.3×.

The right question about an un-verifiable theory-laden input is not whether it is clean but whether the conclusion depends on it; a full 315-point contamination sweep (Te, E, ρm, ν across their literature ranges, worst-case corners included) leaves both observed forebulge offsets bracketed at every point ⇒ ROBUST, so those inputs are not load-bearing and need no bottom-audit; the load-bearing VP-vs-mainstream claims are dimensionless and never use them. # Input-contamination robustness — are the theory-laden geophysical inputs load-bearing?

In plain terms. Some of the numbers fed in — how dense the deep rock is, how thick
and stiff the plate is — aren’t things anyone has directly weighed; they come out of models, and could even
be nudged to fit the standard story. You can’t check them all to the bottom. So instead of asking “are the
numbers exactly right?”, ask “would the answer change if they were wrong?” We took the one test that
leans on those numbers and re-ran it for every combination across the full plausible range — 315 of them.
The answer never changed. So those uncertain numbers don’t carry the result, and there’s no need to verify
them one by one. If the answer had flipped, the test would have said so out loud.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

Tier: methodology (cross-cutting). Sweeps: M35's theory-laden elastic inputs. Firewall: occurrence [O], both directions.

One line. The right question about an un-verifiable theory-laden input is not whether it is clean but
whether the conclusion depends on it; a full 315-point contamination sweep (Te, E, ρm, ν across their
literature ranges, worst-case corners included) leaves both observed forebulge offsets bracketed at every
point ⇒ ROBUST, so those inputs are not load-bearing and need no bottom-audit;
the load-bearing VP-vs-mainstream claims are dimensionless and never use them. Where an input were load-bearing
the same sweep would flag it — verification is delegated and dependency is disclosed, not assumed away.

## 1. The worry — and why "audit everything" is the wrong goal

Some frozen inputs are not observations. Standard crustal density, continental thickness, effective elastic
thickness, mantle density and lithospheric Young’s modulus are theory-laden constructs: an
ensemble-average baked through seismic velocity–density relations (themselves empirical fits) and
isostasy/gravity inversions (non-unique, so a regularisation choice enters). Some may even be quietly corrected toward
a standard picture — importing mainstream assumptions through the back door. Auditing every such input to
the bottom is impossible (even one seismometer trace is unreadable without wave theory and instrument
correction; theory-ladenness has no exit).

So the right question is not “is the input clean?” (unanswerable) but
“does the conclusion depend on the input being clean?” Of dozens of inputs, only a few
actually move a conclusion; a sensitivity sweep — not an exhaustive audit — tells you which. That triages
the infinite-verification problem.

## 2. The hardest case in the cascade

Most load-bearing conclusions never touch these numbers. The area-conservation identity
(M45: dAopen + dAclose = 0) is
purely geometric; the dual-redox result (M42) is a
sign / direction argument. Neither uses density or thickness, so neither can be contaminated by them.
The one place theory-laden geophysical constants do flow into a present-tense conclusion is
M35’s forebulge-position test, which predicts the peripheral
bulge offset from the lithospheric flexural wavelength:

D = E·Te³/(12(1−ν²)),
α = (4D/(ρmg))1/4,
band = [0.5πα, 1.0πα]; tested against observed offsets (US Mid-Atlantic 300 km,
North Sea 250 km). Since α ∝ E1/4·Te3/4·ρm−1/4·(1−ν²)−1/4, the elastic thickness dominates.

## 3. The sweep (pre-registered contamination ranges; no tuning)

The four theory-laden inputs are swept across their full literature spread — Te [40,100] km,
E [50,100] GPa, ρm [3200,3400], ν [0.20,0.30] — over a
315-point grid including every worst-case corner, asking whether both observed offsets stay bracketed
at every point.

| quantity | result over the full hypercube

| flexural parameter α | ranges only [76, 185] km

| grid points with both offsets bracketed | 315 / 315

| Te survival window (even at adversarial corners) | ~[35, 162] km

| plausible cratonic Te range | [40, 100] km — inside the survival window

## 4. Verdict — ROBUST

Across the full contamination hypercube — all four un-verifiable inputs simultaneously at every grid point,
worst-case corners included — both observed forebulge offsets stay bracketed. The conclusion does not
depend on the precise values of Te / E / ρm / ν; it would break only if the elastic
thickness fell below ~35 km or rose above ~160 km, outside the literature range for the cratonic lithosphere
these forebulges sit on. So here the theory-laden inputs are not load-bearing, and auditing them to
the bottom is unnecessary. Had the conclusion flipped inside the ranges, the sweep would have flagged
the dependency rather than hidden it — that is the method.

## 5. Honest scope

This converts a philosophical worry into a verified robustness statement, but it claims exactly
what it shows and no more. M35 is itself
non-discriminating (elasticity is shared by both frameworks), so this is a method
demonstration: even a theory-laden [V] claim is checked for input-dependence rather
than trusted. The genuine residual remains honest: if some input were ever both load-bearing and irreducibly
mainstream-corrected, independence could not be claimed there — the honest move would be to state the
conditional dependency, not bury it. And “frozen” never meant “true”: a SHA-pin
asserts the input is disclosed and replaceable, delegating verification to the reader, who can substitute their
own value and re-derive. Occurrence and absolute ages stay [O], both directions.

## Reproducibility

The screen (repro/robustness_input_contamination_sweep.py) declares the contamination ranges in its LOCK block, sweeps the full 315-point grid, fine-scans the Te survival window at the two adversarial corners, emits a ROBUST / INPUT-DEPENDENT verdict, and proves determinism with a double-SHA-256 self-gate. SEED = 19, no fitted parameter.

2×SHA-256 (ledger body) = b32169721cbfb021f4b6ba9abfb2cd005c3ad8f3b877ed07238c19feee161a5f

python3 repro/robustness_input_contamination_sweep.py → prints the sweep + verdict, recomputes the hash, asserts equality (REPRO GATE: PASS).

Robustness screen complete. The infinite-verification worry is real but the goal — auditing every theory-laden
input — is the wrong one. What is decidable is whether a conclusion depends on an input, and a contamination sweep
decides it: here, ROBUST across 315 worst-case combinations, so the un-verifiable elastic constants are not load-bearing;
elsewhere the load-bearing claims are dimensionless and never touch them. Where a real dependency exists, the method flags
it. Occurrence and absolute ages stay [O]/RECORD, both directions. Falsification = discovery.

# Self-audit — firewall violations found and removed

In plain terms. When the assistant first built part of this strand it claimed it had refuted some strong readings. On review, two of those “refutations” weren't earned by present-day data — they quietly leaned on dated orderings (which the rules forbid) and on a strawman. This page records the mistakes and their corrections, in the open. The discipline caught the auditor.

Author: Young Jae Lee · ORCID 0009-0002-7535-8245 · CC BY 4.0 · https://jamming-physics.org/

This exhibit demonstrates Article 7 in action: every interpretation is checked for being imported, every datum for being recalled rather than recomputed, symmetrically and in both directions.

One line. Two of three claimed “refutations” (M34 glaciation sweep, M37 source-rock origin) are withdrawn as firewall breaches; M38's “Gyr-retention is fine” is corrected with the rock-cycle clock; M36's ×2 is retracted to ~1.2×; M33's all-latitude lock is trimmed; M35's timing is superseded by M44. The corrections remove false refutations without manufacturing false confirmations — the chain returns to its honest standing.

## Method

For every load-bearing claim the question was: is this a present-tense datum, or an imported interpretation (especially a mainstream one) wearing a data costume? A present-tense fact is load-bearing [V]. An absolute date, a rate, a temporal ordering, or a “this is what it means” reading is held out by the firewall ([O]/RECORD).

## Findings, module by module

| Module | Claim audited | Verdict

| M33 | “ice is insolation-locked at ALL latitudes (snowball)” | OVERREACH — toy-EBM artifact; trimmed to the observed high-latitude lock

| M34 | “readvances + hemispheric antiphase refute the clean sweep” | FIREWALL VIOLATION — “leads” is a temporal ordering; refutation RETRACTED → non-discriminating

| M35 | forebulge/marine-limit geometry | CLEAN — present-tense; timing later corrected by M44

| M36 | ×2 enrichment | CLEAN correction — a bad null fixed; retracted to ~1.0–1.3×

| M37 | “laminated source rock refutes a rapid/basal origin” | STRAWMAN + RATE-CLAIM — refutation RETRACTED → non-discriminating on rate

| M38 | “oil survives ~Gyr, no recency edge” | ONE-SIDED — added the rock-cycle clock; Gyr-retention refuted, residence still [O]

| M39 | salt ∝ extension co-variation | CLEAN — already graded non-discriminating

## What changes after the correction

The corrected tally: zero clean present-tense refutations of the framework (the two claimed were artifacts of imported interpretation); four non-discriminating results (M34, M35, M37, M39); one statistical retraction of a VP number (M36, mechanism untouched); one [O] both ways (M38, with honest two-clock reasoning); and one genuine new structural object (the M33 fork plus the observed high-latitude bistable lock). The chain returns to its honest standing — degenerate with mainstream on present-tense axes, [O]-capped on rate/timing, neither confirmed nor refuted. The corrections remove false refutations without manufacturing false confirmations.

## The lesson

The firewall is hardest to keep exactly when importing “mainstream evidence,” because that evidence arrives chronologically framed. Strip every dataset to its present-tense core before it touches the load-bearing column; the ages and orderings stay RECORD — for and against. The framework does not deny the moraines, the laminae, or the oil; it claims a deeper mechanism, and the present-tense data — read without smuggled interpretation — neither refutes nor confirms that mechanism.

Self-audit complete. Falsification = discovery — applied to the auditor's own work. The corrections are recorded mark-never-erase; the strand's modules carry each one inline.

## Owned by this volume (canonical here)

### Dual-redox petroleum mechanism [V]
Glacial meltwater does opposite things to oxygen at two depths: sealing it out deep (preserving source rock) and bringing it in shallow (making oil heavy); reproduces oil quality across 6/6 provinces (M42).

### Freshwater-lid anoxia [V]
A layer of fresh meltwater sitting on heavier seawater stops oxygen reaching the bottom → the bottom goes anoxic → organic matter is preserved (the source-rock preservation half of the dual-redox).
value present-tense · owner recent-sequence-cascade
canonical: ../modules/28_source_rock_organic_richness.html

### Biodegradation [V]
Microbes eat the light fractions of oil in cool, shallow, oxygen-reached reservoirs, leaving it heavy; the process shuts off above ~80 °C.
